Shaykh al-Islam mentioned, from the narration of al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim from him, that he said: "Allah created the Throne first of all created things, and then He established Himself upon it." I say: This is in the tafsir of al-Dahhak. In the tafsir of al-Suddi, from Abu Malik and Abu Salih from Ibn Abbas, concerning ﴿The Most Merciful established Himself upon the Throne﴾ [Ta-Ha: 5], he said: "He sat (qa'ada)."

[The statement of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him]

Abu al-Shaykh related in the Book of al-Azamah from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "A man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what is al-Haqqa?' He said: 'The day when the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, descends upon His Throne.'"

Al-Bukhari said in the Book of the Creation of the Actions of the Servants: Ibn Mas'ud said concerning the Exalted's saying: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven﴾ [Fussilat: 11] and His saying: ﴿Then He established Himself upon the Throne﴾ [Al-A'raf: 54]: "The Throne is upon the water, and Allah is above the Throne, and He knows what you are upon." Ibn Mas'ud also said: "Whoever says: 'Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and there is no god but Allah, and Allah is the Greatest,' an angel receives them and ascends with them to Allah. He does not pass by any assembly of angels except that they ask forgiveness for the one who said them, until he brings them to the Face of the Most Merciful." Al-Assal related it in the Book of Knowledge (al-Ma'rifa) with a chain whose narrators are all trustworthy (thiqat). Al-Darimi said: Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us, from al-Zubayr ibn Abd al-Salam, from Ayyub ibn Abdullah al-Fihri, that Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Indeed your Lord has no night or day with Him. The light of the heavens and the earth is from the light of His Face. The measure of each of your days with Him is twelve hours. Your deeds of yesterday are presented to Him at the beginning of the day, today. He looks into them for three hours, and He discovers in them that which He dislikes, and that angers Him. The first to know of His anger are those who carry the Throne. They find it heavy upon them, so those who carry the Throne glorify Him, and the enclosures of the Throne and the near angels and the rest of the angels [glorify Him]." This is longer in the Mu'jam of al-Tabarani.

It is authentically reported from al-Suddi, from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from Abu Malik and Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, and from Murrah, from some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), concerning the saying: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven﴾ [Fussilat: 11], that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, was upon His Throne over the water, and He had not created anything before the water. . . the hadith. In it: "When He finished creating what He willed, He established Himself upon the Throne." And this does not contradict the hadith: "The first thing Allah created was the pen," for two reasons. The first: the firstness refers to its writing, not to its creation, for the hadith says: "The first thing Allah created was the pen. He said to it: 'Write.' It said: 'What shall I write?' He said: 'Write what will be until the Day of Resurrection.'" The second: the intended meaning is the first thing Allah created in this world after the creation of the Throne, for the Throne was created before it according to the more correct of the two statements of the Salaf, both of which were related by the memorizer Abd al-Qadir al-Rahawi. The precedence of the creation of the Throne is shown by his saying in the established hadith: "Allah decreed the measures of the creatures fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth, and His Throne was upon the water."

Ibn al-Qayyim said in his commentary on Surah 32, verses 4–6 (part 14 of 15):

He has informed that when He created the Pen, He decreed the destinies by it, as in the other wording: "He said: Write. It said: What shall I write? He said: Write the decree (al-qadar)." This is the time-bound decree before the creation of the world by fifty thousand years. Thus it is established that the Throne preceded the Pen, and the Throne was upon the water before the creation of the heavens and the earth. So the statements of the Companions do not contradict what the Messenger ﷺ reported. Abu al-Qasim al-Lalika'i narrated with a sound chain from Khaythama, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "Indeed, a servant may resolve upon a matter of trade or leadership, until when it is made easy for him, Allah looks at him from above the seven heavens, and says to the angels: Turn him away from it, for if I make it easy for him, I will admit him to the Fire."

A similar report has preceded from Ibn Abbas, both as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet ﷺ) and as a mawquf (ending with a Companion). Sunayd ibn Dawud mentioned, with a sound chain from him, that he said: "The distance between the heaven and the earth is a journey of five hundred years, and the distance between each heaven and the next is a journey of five hundred years, and the distance between the seventh heaven and the Kursi is a journey of five hundred years. The Throne is upon the water, and Allah the Exalted is upon the Throne, and He knows your deeds."

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Ubayda, who said: Abdullah said: "Show mercy to those on the earth, and He who is in the heaven will show mercy to you." Hammad ibn Salama said, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from al-Sha'bi, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Indeed Allah has filled the Throne, so that it has a creaking like the creaking of a saddle..." Harb narrated it from Ishaq, from Rawh, from Adam ibn Abi Iyas, from Hammad.

[The statement of Mujahid and Abu al-'Aliya]

Al-Bayhaqi narrated through the route of Shibl, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And We brought him near as a confidant﴾ [Maryam: 52], that he said: "Between the seventh heaven and the Throne there are seventy thousand veils. He kept bringing Musa closer until there was only one veil between him and Him. When he saw His place and heard the scratching of the Pen, he said: My Lord, show me, let me look at You."

Al-Bukhari said in his Sahih: Abu al-'Aliya said: "Istawa ila al-sama'" means He rose (irtafa'a). Mujahid said: "Istawa" means He rose above (ala) the Throne. Mujahid also said regarding the words of the Exalted: ﴿Then there succeeded them a generation who neglected prayer and followed desires﴾ [Maryam: 59], that they are in this Ummah, mounting one another as donkeys and livestock mount one another on the roads, not feeling shame before people on earth, and not fearing Allah in the heaven. Al-Haytham ibn Khalaf al-Duri narrated it in the book Tahrim al-Liwat.

[The statement of Qatada]

What Uthman al-Darimi narrated from him in the book al-Naqd has already been mentioned, where he said: The Children of Israel said: "O Lord, You are in the heaven and we are on the earth, so how can we know Your pleasure and Your anger?" He said: "When I am pleased with you, I appoint over you your best, and when I am angry with you, I appoint over you your worst."

In the Tafsir of Ibn Abi Hatim, from Qatada, he said: "Then He istawa upon the Throne on Friday."

[The statement of Ikrima]

Authentically reported from Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam, from his father, from Ikrima, who said: "While a man was in Paradise, he said to himself: If Allah permitted me, I would plant. Then the angels at the gates of his Paradise say to him: Peace be upon you. Your Lord says to you: You have wished for something and you have known it. He has sent with us the seed, and says to you: Sow. So it grows like mountains. Then the Lord from above His Throne says to him: Eat, O son of Adam, for the son of Adam is never satisfied." It has a supporting marfu' report in Sahih al-Bukhari.

[The statement of Sa'id ibn Jubayr]

He narrated from him through several routes, who said: People suffered a drought in the time of one of the kings of the Children of Israel. The king said: "Allah will surely send down the sky upon us, or we will harm Him." His companions said: "How can you, when He is in the sky?" He said: "I will kill His friends." So Allah sent the sky upon them.

[The statement of al-Dahhak]

It has already been mentioned from him regarding the words of the Exalted: ﴿There is no secret conference of three but that He is their fourth﴾ [al-Mujadila: 7] that he said: "He is upon His Throne, and His knowledge is with them." Ibn Battah, Ibn Abd al-Barr and al-Assal mentioned it in the book al-Ma'rifa, and its wording is: "He is above His Throne, and His knowledge is with them wherever they are." Ahmad narrated it from Nuh ibn Maymun, from Bakr ibn Ma'ruf, from Muqatil, from him, with the wording: "He is upon the Throne and His knowledge is with them." Ibn Abd al-Barr reported the consensus of the Companions and the Successors upon this.

[The statements of the ascetics and Sufis of the followers and their predecessors]

[The statement of Thabit al-Bunani, shaykh of the ascetics]

Muhammad ibn Uthman said in his Risala: It is authentically reported from him that he said: "Dawud, peace be upon him, used to prolong the prayer, then bow, then raise his head to the sky and say: To You I raised my head, like the gaze of slaves toward their masters, O Dweller of the heaven." Al-Lalika'i narrated it with a sound chain from him, and Imam Ahmad also narrated it in the book al-Zuhd. This raising, if it was during the prayer, then it is abrogated in our law; and if it was after the prayer, then it is permissible, like raising the hands in supplication to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

[The statement of Malik ibn Dinar]

We have already cited from him that he used to say: "Take..." then he recites, then says: "Listen to the words of the Truthful from above His Throne." Abu Nu'aym narrated it in al-Hilya with a sound chain from him. Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated from him, who said: "I read in some books that Allah the Exalted says: O son of Adam, My good comes down to you and your evil ascends to Me. I make Myself beloved to you with favors, and you make yourself hateful to Me with sins. A noble angel does not cease to ascend to Me from you with an ugly deed."

[The statement of Sulayman al-Taymi]

Al-Bukhari said in the book Khalq Af'al al-'Ibad: Damra ibn Rabi'a narrated from Sadaqa, from Sulayman, I heard him say: "If I were asked: Where is Allah? I would say: In the heaven. If I were asked: Where was the Throne before He created the heaven? I would say: Upon the water. If I were asked: Where was His Throne before He created the water? I would say: I do not know."

[The statement of Shurayh ibn Ubayd]

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from him with a sound chain that he used to say: "The praise of glorification has risen to You, and the dignity of holiness has ascended to You. Glory be to You, O Possessor of majesty; in Your hand is the dominion, the kingdom, the keys and the decrees."

[The statement of Ubayd ibn Umayr]

Abdullah ibn Ahmad narrated in his book al-Sunna, from the hadith of Hajjaj, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata', from Ubayd ibn Umayr, that he said: "The Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, descends at the middle of the night to the lowest heaven and says: Who will ask Me so I may give to him? Who will seek My forgiveness so I may forgive him? Until when dawn comes, the Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, ascends."

[The statement of Fudayl ibn Iyad]

Al-Athram said in the book al-Sunna: Ibrahim ibn al-Harith, meaning al-'Ubbadi, narrated to us. Al-Layth ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: I heard Ibrahim ibn al-Ash'ath say: Abu Bakr, companion of Fudayl, said: I heard Fudayl ibn Iyad say: "It is not for us to imagine about Allah how and how, because Allah described Himself most eloquently, saying: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born, nor is there to Him any equivalent.﴾ [al-Ikhlas: 1-4] There is no description more eloquent than what Allah described Himself with. Likewise the descent, laughter, boasting and looking down, as He wills to descend, as He wills to boast, (and as He wills to look down), and as He wills to laugh. So it is not for us to imagine how and how. And if the Jahmi says to you: I disbelieve in a Lord who moves from His place, then you say: I believe in a Lord who does whatever He wills." Al-Bukhari also mentioned this last statement from Fudayl in the book Khalq al-Af'al, saying: "Fudayl ibn Iyad said: If the Jahmi says to you..." and then mentioned it.

[The statement of Yahya ibn Mu'adh al-Razi]

He said: Allah the Exalted is upon the Throne, separate from creation, having encompassed everything in knowledge and counted everything in number. None doubts this statement except a wicked, misguided, perished, doubting Jahmi who says: Allah is mixed with His creation, and mingles the Essence with filth and stench.

[The statement of Ata al-Sulami]

It is established that he would not raise his head to the sky out of shame before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. From this is the Prophet's ﷺ prohibition of the one praying from raising his gaze to the sky, out of courtesy toward Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and lowering the gaze before Him, and reverence for Him, as slaves stand before kings and do not raise their heads to them out of reverence for them. When this is combined with raising the hands in desires and fears, and the turning of hearts toward the height, not to the right, left, behind or in front, it establishes knowledge that this is the innate nature (fitra) of Allah with which He created mankind.

[The statement of Abu Ubayda al-Khawwas]

Abu Nu'aym and Ibn al-Jawzi mentioned from him that he remained so-and-so many years without raising his head to the sky, out of shame before Allah.

[The statement of Bishr al-Hafi]

Authentically reported from him that he said: "Indeed I raise my hands to Allah, then return them, and say: Only one who has standing (jah) with Allah does this."

[The statement of Dhu al-Nun al-Misri]

Abu al-Shaykh narrated in the book al-'Azama with his chain from him, who said: "The heavens were illuminated by His light, the darknesses were lit by His face, His majesty was veiled from the eyes, and the tongues of hearts whispered to Him upon His Throne." (If it is said): al-Qushayri has transmitted from Dhu al-Nun that he was asked about the words of the Exalted: ﴿The Merciful is established upon the Throne﴾ [Ta-Ha: 5], and he said: "He affirmed His essence and negated His place, so He exists in His essence, and things exist by His wisdom as He wills." It was said: al-Qushayri did not give a chain for this report, while what we have mentioned is transmitted from him with a chain. In the books of Sufism there are fabricated accounts, and Allah knows best about them. Shaykh al-Islam said: This transmission is baseless, for this statement has no relevance to the verse; rather it contradicts it, since this verse does not include affirming His essence and negating His place in any way. How then is it interpreted by that? He said: As for his saying that He exists in His essence and things exist by His judgment, this is true, but it is not the meaning of the verse.

[The statement of al-Harith ibn Asad al-Muhasibi]

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 32, verses 4–6 (part 15 of 15):

He said: As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The Most Merciful is established upon the Throne﴾ [Ta-Ha: 5], ﴿And He is the Subduer over His servants﴾ [al-An'am: 18], ﴿Are you secure from the One who is in the heaven?﴾ [al-Mulk: 16], ﴿Then they would have sought a way to the Owner of the Throne﴾ [al-Isra': 42], these and others like them, and His saying: ﴿The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 4], ﴿To Him ascends the good word﴾ [Fatir: 10]: all of this necessitates that He is above the Throne, above all things, transcendent above entering into His creation, nothing of them concealed from Him. For He made clear in these verses that He intended that He Himself is above His servants, since He said: ﴿Are you secure from the One who is in the heaven, that He will cause the earth to swallow you?﴾ [al-Mulk: 16], meaning: above the Throne, and the Throne is above the heaven, because the One who is above everything is above the heaven, in the heaven. And He has said: ﴿So travel in the earth for four months﴾ [al-Tawbah: 2], meaning: upon the earth, not intending entry into its interior. Likewise His saying: ﴿They wander in the earth﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 26], meaning: upon the earth. Likewise His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And I will surely crucify you upon the trunks of palm trees﴾ [Ta-Ha: 71], meaning: upon them, on them. And He said in another place: "So He made clear" the ascent of the command and the ascent of the angels. Then He described the time of their ascent by its being an elevation, rising toward Him, so He said: ﴿In a Day whose extent is fifty thousand years﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 4]. Thus He mentioned their ascent to Him and their arrival at Him by His saying "to Him," like the saying of one who says: "Ascend to so-and-so in a night or a day," because He is in the high place, and your ascent to Him takes a day. So when they ascend to the Throne, they have ascended to Allah, mighty and majestic, even if they have not seen Him and have not equaled Him in elevation. For they ascended from the earth and went up with the command to the height above which Allah, exalted is He, is. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Rather, Allah raised him to Himself﴾ [al-Nisa': 158]; He did not say: "near Him." And Pharaoh said: ﴿O Haman, build for me a tower that perhaps I may reach the means, the means of the heavens, and look at the God of Moses﴾ [Ghafir: 36–37]. Then he resumed and said: ﴿And indeed, I think him a liar﴾ [Ghafir: 37], meaning: in what he said, that his God is above the heavens. So Allah, mighty and majestic, made clear that Pharaoh suspected Moses of lying in what he told him, and he resorted to seeking Him, since he said to him, along with the suspicion of Moses, that he was a liar. And if Moses had said that He is in every place by His essence, he would have sought Him in his house or his latrine. Allah is exalted above that by a great exaltation. And he did not exert himself by building the tower.

[The saying of the leading Sufi of his time, the gnostic imam Abu 'Abd Allah 'Amr ibn 'Uthman al-Makki]

(The saying of the leading Sufi of his time): The gnostic imam Abu 'Abd Allah 'Amr ibn 'Uthman al-Makki said in his book Adab al-Muridin wa al-Ta'arruf bi Ahwal al-'Ibad ("The Etiquette of Disciples and Knowledge of the States of the Servants") ... in the chapter on what Satan brings to "the repentant" of whispering. As for the third aspect with which people come when they refuse him and take refuge in Allah, he whispers to them concerning the matter of the Creator, to corrupt for them the foundations of tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness). He mentioned a lengthy discourse until he said: This is among the greatest things with which he whispers concerning tawhid, by casting doubt, and concerning the attributes of the Lord by likening and comparison, or by denying them and ta'til (denial of divine attributes), and by introducing to them measures of the Lord's greatness according to their intellects, so that they perish (if they accept) or their pillars are shaken, unless they resort in that to knowledge and the realization of gnosis of Allah, mighty and majestic, from the perspective of what He informed about Himself, described Himself with, and what His Messenger described Him with. For He, exalted is He, is the One who says: "I am Allah," not the tree, nor its ... He is established upon His Throne with the greatness of His majesty, apart from every place, the One who spoke to Moses with direct speech and showed him of His great signs. Moses heard the speech of Allah, the Inheritor of His creation, the Hearer of their voices, who sees their bodies with His eye. His two hands are outstretched, and they are other than His blessing and His power. He created Adam with His hand. Then he went on with a lengthy discourse in the Sunnah. He, may Allah have mercy on him, was among the peers of al-Junayd and the notables of the shaykhs of the people. He died in the year 291 AH in Baghdad.

[The saying of Abu Ja'far al-Hamadani the Sufi]

Muhammad ibn Tahir al-Maqdisi, the Sufi hadith scholar, mentioned in his book, from him, that he attended the session of Abu al-Ma'ali al-Juwayni while he was saying: "Allah was, and there was no Throne, and He is now as He was." ... and words of this meaning. So he (al-Hamadani) said: "O Shaykh, leave us from mentioning the Throne and inform us about this necessity that we find in our hearts, for no gnostic has ever said 'O Allah' except that he finds in his heart a necessity seeking elevation, not turning right or left. So how do we repel this necessity from our hearts?" He said: Then Abu al-Ma'ali cried out, slapped his head, and said: "Al-Hamadani has bewildered me! Al-Hamadani has bewildered me!"

[The saying of the gnostic imam Ma'mar ibn Ahmad al-Isbahani]

The shaykh of the Sufis at the end of the fourth century (AH). He said in a treatise: "I wished to counsel my companions with a counsel from the Sunnah and an admonition from wisdom, and to gather what the people of hadith and transmission, and the people of gnosis and Sufism, from the earlier and later generations, held." He said in it: Allah is established upon His Throne without modality, without likening, without ta'wil (figurative interpretation). The establishment is intelligible, and the modality is unknown. He, mighty and majestic, is separate from His creation, and the creation is separate from Him, without indwelling, without mixing, without intermingling, without adjacency. For He is the Unique, separate from creation, the One, free of need for creation. Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing, All-Knowing, All-Aware. He speaks, is pleased, is angry, laughs, wonders, and manifests Himself to His servants on the Day of Resurrection laughing, and He descends every night to the lowest heaven as He wills, so He says: "Is there anyone calling upon Me that I may answer him? Is there anyone repenting that I may accept his repentance? Is there anyone asking forgiveness that I may forgive him?" until the dawn rises. And the descent of the Lord to the heaven is without modality, without likening, without ta'wil. Whoever denies the descent or interprets it, he is an innovator and astray.

[The saying of the shaykh, the gnostic imam, leader of the gnostics, Shaykh 'Abd al-Qadir al-Jilani]

May Allah sanctify his spirit. He said in his book Tuhfat al-Muttaqin wa Sabil al-'Arifin ("The Gift of the God-fearing and the Way of the Gnostics"), in the chapter on the differences of the schools concerning the attributes of Allah, mighty and majestic, and in mentioning the people's disagreement about the pause at His saying: ﴿And none knows its interpretation except Allah and those firm in knowledge﴾ [Al 'Imran: 7]. He continued until he said: Allah, exalted is He, is by His essence upon the Throne, and His knowledge encompasses every place. The pause according to the people of truth is at His saying: ﴿except Allah﴾ [Al 'Imran: 7]. This has been narrated from Fatimah, daughter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). And this pause is good for one who believes that Allah, by His essence, is above the Throne and knows what is in the heavens and the earth. He continued: A group of those who deny the establishment of the Lord, mighty and majestic, paused at His saying: ﴿The Most Merciful is established upon the Throne﴾ [Ta-Ha: 5], and began with His saying: ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ [Ta-Ha: 6], intending by that to negate the establishment with which He described Himself. This is an error on their part, for Allah, exalted is He, is established upon the Throne by His essence.

He said in his book al-Ghunyah: As for knowing the Creator through signs and proofs in summary, it is that you know and are certain that Allah is One, the Unique, ... and He is in the direction of height, established upon the Throne, possessing dominion, His knowledge encompassing things: ﴿To Him ascends the good word, and righteous deed He raises﴾ [Fatir: 10]. (He directs the affair from the heaven to the earth, then it ascends to Him in a Day whose extent is a thousand years of what you count.) [al-Sajdah: 5]

So it is not permissible to describe Him as being in every place. Rather it is said: He is in the heaven, "established upon the Throne," as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿The Most Merciful is established upon the Throne﴾ [Ta-Ha: 5]. He then cited verses and hadiths. Then he said: It is appropriate to affirm the attribute of establishment without ta'wil, and that it is the establishment of the Essence upon the Throne. Then he said: That He is upon the Throne is mentioned in every book sent down to every prophet sent, without modality. This is the text of his words in al-Ghunyah.

**[Refutation of the Heretics and the Deniers]**

Reflect on what these verses contain by way of refutation of the sects of the deniers (*al-Mu'attilah*) and the polytheists. His words, ﴿He created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days﴾, include the refutation of the statement of the heretics (*al-Malahidah*) who hold that the world is eternal, that it has always existed, and that God, glorified is He, did not create it by His power and will. As for those among them who affirmed the existence of the Lord, they made Him necessarily joined to His essence, first and forever, uncreated, as is the view of Ibn Sina, al-Nasir al-Tusi and their followers among the heretics, who deny what the Messengers, upon them be prayers and peace, the Books agreed upon, and what the intellects and natural dispositions (*fitan*) bear witness to.

His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Then He istawa over the Throne﴾ include the refutation of the statement of the deniers (*al-Mu'attilah*) and the Jahmiyyah, who say: "There is nothing above the Throne but nothingness," and that God is not established (*mustawin*) upon His Throne, that hands are not raised to Him, that the good word does not ascend to Him, that Allah did not raise the Messiah, upon him be peace, to Himself, that His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) was not ascended "to Him," that the angels and the Spirit do not ascend to Him, that Gabriel, upon him be peace, and others do not descend from Him, that He does not descend every night to the lowest heaven, and that His servants among the angels and others do not fear Him from above them, and that the believers will not see Him in the Hereafter with their eyes from above them. It is also not permitted to point with the fingers upward toward Him, as the Prophet (ﷺ) did at the greatest of his gatherings, at the Farewell Pilgrimage, when he began raising his finger to the sky and lowering it toward the people, saying: "O Allah, bear witness."

**[Affirmation of Allah's Istiwa' over His Throne from the Book]**

The Shaykh al-Islam said: "This is the Book of Allah from its beginning to its end, and the Sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ), and most of the words of the Companions and the Followers, and the words of all the Imams, are filled with what is explicit or apparent in showing that Allah, glorified and exalted, is above everything, that He is above the Throne, above the heavens, established upon His Throne. Such as His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿To Him ascends the good word, and righteous deed He raises up﴾ [Fatir: 10], and His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿When Allah said: O Isa, indeed I will take you and raise you to Myself﴾ [Al 'Imran: 55], and His words: ﴿But Allah raised him to Himself﴾ [al-Nisa': 158], and His words: (. . . . . . . . . ﴿Owner of the ascending stairways. The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 3], and His words: ﴿He arranges the affair from the heaven to the earth; then it ascends to Him﴾ [al-Sajdah: 5], and His words: ﴿They fear their Lord from above them﴾ [al-Nahl: 50], and His words: ﴿It is He who created for you all that is on the earth, then He istawa toward the heaven and made them seven heavens﴾ [al-Baqarah: 29], and His words: ﴿Indeed your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days; then He istawa over the Throne, covering the night with the day, which it follows rapidly, and the sun and the moon and the stars subjected by His command. Unquestionably, to Him belong creation and command. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-A'raf: 54], and His words: ﴿Indeed your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days; then He istawa over the Throne, arranging the affair. There is no intercessor except after His permission. That is Allah, your Lord, so worship Him. Will you not remember?﴾ [Yunus: 3]. In this verse He mentioned both monotheisms.

And His words: ﴿A revelation from He who created the earth and the high heavens, the Most Merciful, who istawa over the Throne﴾ [Ta-Ha: 4].

And His words: ﴿And rely upon the Living who does not die, and glorify Him with His praise, and sufficient is He with the sins of His servants, Aware. He who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days; then He istawa over the Throne, the Most Merciful. So ask about Him one who is aware﴾ [al-Furqan: 58].

And His words: ﴿It is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days; then He istawa over the Throne. He knows what enters into the earth and what emerges from it, what descends from the sky and what ascends into it. And He is with you wherever you are. And Allah sees what you do﴾ [al-Hadid: 4]. So He mentioned the generality of His knowledge, the generality of His power, the generality of His encompassing, and the generality of His seeing.

And His words: ﴿Do you feel secure that He who is in the heaven will not cause the earth to swallow you while it shakes? Or do you feel secure that He who is in the heaven will not send upon you a storm of stones? Then you will know how My warning was﴾ [al-Mulk: 16]. And His words: ﴿A revelation from the All-Wise, Praiseworthy﴾ [Fussilat: 42], and His words: ﴿The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise﴾ [al-Zumar: 1], and His words: ﴿And Pharaoh said: O Haman, build for me a tower that I may reach the ways, the ways of the heavens, and look at the God of Moses; and indeed I think he is a liar﴾ [Ghafir: 36–37].

Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari said: "This verse has been used as an argument against the Jahmiyyah, for Pharaoh denied Moses, upon him be peace, in his saying that Allah is 'above' the heavens. The narration of his words, word for word, will come, Allah willing."

**[Affirmation of Allah's Istiwa' over His Throne from the Sunnah]**

As for the hadiths, among them is the story of the Mi'raj (Night Journey and Ascension), which is *mutawatir* (narrated by so many chains that its truth is certain), and the Prophet (ﷺ) passing through the "heavens," heaven after heaven, until he reached his Lord, the Exalted, and He drew him near and brought him close, and prescribed upon him the prayers, fifty prayers. He kept going back and forth between Moses, upon him be peace, and his Lord, blessed and exalted. He would descend from his Lord to Moses, and Moses would ask him how many were prescribed for him, and he would inform him, and Moses would say: "Return to your Lord and ask Him for lightening," so he would ascend to his Lord and ask Him for lightening.

In the two Sahihs (Bukhari and Muslim), from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah created the creation, He wrote in His Book, which is with Him above the Throne: 'Indeed My mercy overcomes My anger.'" In another wording: "He wrote in His Book concerning Himself, and it is placed with Him: 'Indeed My mercy overcomes My anger.'" And in another wording: "It was placed with Him upon the Throne." And in another wording: "It is written with Him above the Throne." All these wordings are authentic in Sahih al-Bukhari and Muslim.

And in Sahih Muslim, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood among us and spoke five words: "Indeed Allah does not sleep, and it is not fitting for Him to sleep. He lowers the scale and raises it. The deeds of the night are raised to Him before the deeds of the day, and the deeds of the day before the deeds of the night. His veil is light; if He were to unveil it, the splendors of His face would burn whatever of His creation His sight reaches."

Al-Bukhari mentioned in the Book of Tawhid in his Sahih the hadith of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, the hadith of the Isra' (Night Journey), and in it: "Then he (Gabriel) ascended with him above that with what none knows except Allah, until he passed the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary, and the Majestic, the Lord of Might, drew near and came down, until he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or nearer. He revealed to him what He revealed: fifty prayers upon your nation every day and night. Then he descended until he reached Moses, who detained him and said: 'O Muhammad, what did your Lord charge you with?' He said: 'He charged me with fifty prayers every day and night.' He said: 'Indeed your nation cannot bear that. Return, and your Lord will lighten it for you and for them.' The Prophet (ﷺ) turned to Gabriel as if seeking his counsel about that, and Gabriel signaled to him: 'Yes, if you wish.' So he ascended with him to the Majestic, blessed and exalted, and he said, while in his place: 'O Lord, lighten it for us...' and he mentioned the hadith."

In the two Sahihs, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Angels succeed one another among you by night and angels by day, and they gather at the 'Asr prayer and the Fajr prayer. Then those who spent the night among you ascend, and He asks them—and He is most knowing of them—'How did you leave My servants?' They say: 'We left them while they were praying, and we came to them while they were praying.'"

When Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, may Allah be pleased with him, judged concerning Banu Qurayzah that their fighting men be killed, their children taken captive, and their wealth divided, the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "You have judged among them by the judgment of Allah from above seven layers"; and in another wording: "from above seven heavens."

The origin of this story is in the two Sahihs, and this wording is that of Muhammad ibn Ishaq in *al-Maghazi*.

In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "Ali ibn Abi Talib sent to the Prophet (ﷺ) a gold nugget in a piece of leather, not yet separated from its earth. He divided it among four: 'Uyaynah ibn Badr, al-Aqra' ibn Habis, Zayd al-Khayl, and the fourth was either 'Alqamah ibn 'Ulathah or 'Amir ibn al-Tufayl." A man from among his Companions said: "We were more deserving of this than these." When that reached the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "Will you not trust me, when I am the trusted one of Him who is in the heaven? The news of the heaven comes to me morning and evening."

In Sahih Muslim, from Mu'awiyah ibn al-Hakam al-Sulami, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "I slapped a slave-girl of mine, and I informed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he considered that a great matter for me. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, shall I not free her?' He said: 'Yes, bring her to me.' So I brought her to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said to her: 'Where is Allah?' She said: 'In the heaven.' He said: 'Who am I?' She said: 'You are the Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'Free her, for she is a believer.'"

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Zaynab, may Allah be pleased with her, used to boast over the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) and say: "Your families married you off, but Allah married me from above seven heavens."

In Sunan Abi Dawud, from the hadith of Jubayr ibn Mut'im, who said: "A Bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, souls have been exhausted, dependents have gone hungry, wealth has been depleted, and livestock has perished. So ask Allah for rain for us, for we seek your intercession with Allah and we seek Allah's intercession with you.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Woe to you! Do you know what you are saying?' And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) glorified Allah and kept glorifying until that was recognized in the faces of his Companions. Then he said: 'Woe to you! Allah is not sought as an intercessor with anyone of His creation; the affair of Allah is greater than that. Woe to you! Do you know what Allah is? Indeed His Throne is over His heavens, like this,' and he gestured with his fingers like a dome over it, 'and it creaks with Him like the creaking of a saddle with its rider.'"

Also in Sunan Abi Dawud and Musnad al-Imam Ahmad, from the hadith of al-Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "I was in al-Batha' in a group in which was the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when a cloud passed over them. He looked at it and said: 'What do you call this?' They said: 'The cloud (*sahab*).' He said: 'And the rain-cloud (*muzn*).' They said: 'And the rain-cloud.' He said: 'And the dense cloud (*'anan*).' They said: 'And the dense cloud.' He said: 'Do you know how far is the distance between the heaven and the earth?' They said: 'We do not know.' He said: 'Indeed the distance between them is either one, or two, or three and seventy years. Then the heaven above it is likewise,' until he counted seven heavens. 'Then above the seventh is a sea, between whose upper and lower parts is like the distance between one heaven and another. Then above that are eight mountain goats, between whose hooves and knees is like the distance between one heaven and another. Then upon their backs is the Throne, between whose lower and upper parts is like the distance between one heaven and another. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, is above that.'" Ahmad added: "Nothing of the deeds of the sons of Adam is hidden from Him."

And in the Sunan of Abu Dawud as well, from Fadalah ibn Ubayd, from Abu al-Darda (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever among you suffers from something, or a brother of his suffers from it, let him say: 'Our Lord is Allah, who is in the heaven. Your name is sanctified. Your command is in the heaven and the earth, as Your mercy is in the heaven, so place Your mercy on the earth. Forgive us our sin and our wrongdoings. You are the Lord of the good ones. Send down mercy from Your mercy and healing from Your healing upon this "pain," and he will be healed.'"

And in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him): "A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) with a black, non-Arab slave girl and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, upon me is a believing slave to be freed.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to her: 'Where is Allah?' She pointed with her index finger to the sky. He said to her: 'Who am I?' She pointed with her finger to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and to the sky, meaning: You are the Messenger of Allah. He said: 'Free her.'"

In the Jami' of al-Tirmidhi, from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Those who show mercy will be shown mercy by the All-Merciful. Show mercy to those on the earth, and the One in the heaven will show mercy to you." Al-Tirmidhi said: this is a hadith that is hasan sahih (good and authentic). And in it also, from Imran ibn Husayn, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to my father: 'O Husayn, how many gods do you worship today?' My father said: 'Seven: six on the earth and one in the heaven.' He said: 'Which of them do you prepare for your desire and your fear?' He said: 'The One who is in the heaven.' He said: 'O Husayn, as for you, if you were to accept Islam, I would teach you two words that would benefit you.' When Husayn accepted Islam, he came and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, teach me the two words you promised me.' He said: 'Say: O Allah, inspire me with my right guidance and protect me from the evil of my soul.'"

And in Sahih Muslim, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By He in whose hand is my soul, there is no man who calls his wife to his bed and she refuses him, except that the One who is in the heaven is angry with her until he is pleased with her."

And al-Shafi'i narrated in his Musnad, from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "Jibril came to the Prophet (ﷺ) with a white mirror in his palm, in which there was a black spot. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'What is this, O (Jibril)?' He said: 'This is Friday, with which you and your nation have been favored. The people are followers of you in it: the Jews and the Christians. For you there is good in it, and in it there is an hour in which no believer who asks Allah for good coincides with it except that he is answered. It is with us the Day of Increase.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'O Jibril, what is the Day of Increase?' He said: 'Your Lord has taken in Paradise a wide valley, in which there are dunes of musk. When it is the day of Friday, Allah, blessed and exalted, sends down whichever of His angels He wills, and around Him are pulpits of light, upon which are the seats of the Prophets. Those pulpits are surrounded by pulpits of gold, adorned with rubies and chrysolite, upon which are the martyrs and the truthful ones. They sit behind them on those dunes. Allah, mighty and majestic, says: I am your Lord, and I have truly fulfilled My promise to you. Ask Me and I will give you.' They say: 'Our Lord, we ask You for Your pleasure.' He says: 'I am pleased with you, and for you is whatever you wished, and with Me there is more.' So they love the day of Friday because of the good their Lord gives them in it. It is the day on which your Lord, glorified and exalted, established Himself over the Throne, and in it Adam was created, and in it the Hour will come.'"

For this hadith there are several chains, which Abu Bakr ibn Abi Dawud collected in a juz' (a small volume). And in the Sunan of Ibn Majah, from the hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "While the people of Paradise are in their bliss, a light shines upon them, and they raise their heads, and behold, the Lord, exalted, has looked down upon them from above and said: 'Peace be upon you, O people of Paradise.'" He said: That is His saying, exalted: ﴿Peace, a word from a Lord, Most Merciful﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:58]. He said: "He looks at them and they look at Him, and they do not turn to anything of the bliss as long as they are looking at Him, until He veils Himself from them, and His light and blessing remain upon them in their homes."

And in the two Sahihs (Bukhari and Muslim), from the hadith of Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever gives charity equal to a date from lawful earnings, and nothing good ascends to Allah except the good, Allah receives it with His right hand, then He nurtures it for its giver just as one of you nurtures his foal, until it becomes like a mountain."

In the Sahih of Ibn Hibban, on the authority of Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, from Salman al-Farisi, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed your Lord is Modest and Generous. He is shy before His servant when the servant raises his hands to Him that He should return them empty, with nothing in them."

Ibn Wahb narrated: Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub informed me, from Zuhra ibn Ma'bad, from Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he heard Uqba ibn Amir, may Allah be pleased with him, say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever performs wudu' and does it well, then raises his gaze to the sky and says: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger,' the eight gates of Paradise will be opened for him, and he may enter through whichever of them he wishes."

In the lengthy hadith of intercession, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Then I will enter upon my Lord, blessed and exalted, while He is upon His Throne," and he mentioned the hadith. In one of the wordings in the Sahih of al-Bukhari: "Then I will ask permission to enter upon my Lord in His abode, and I will be permitted to enter upon Him." Abd al-Haqq said in al-Jam' bayna al-Sahihayn: "Thus he said, 'in His abode,' in the three places," meaning the three places of intercession in which he prostrates and then raises his head.

Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Umawi narrated in his Maghazi, through the route of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: "A black slave belonging to one of the people of Khaybar went out until he came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'Who is this?' They said: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' He said: 'The One who is in the sky?' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Are you the Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'The One who is in the sky?' He said: 'Yes.' So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded him to bear witness to the shahada, and he testified, then fought until he was martyred."

Adi ibn Umayra al-Kindi narrated, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) related from his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, that He said: "By My might, My majesty, and My exaltation above My Throne, there is no people of a town, nor a house, nor a man in the desert, who were upon what I dislike of My disobedience and then turned away from it to what I love of My obedience, except that I will turn for them from what they dislike of My punishment to what they love of My mercy." Ibn Abi Shayba narrated it in Kitab al-'Arsh, and Abu Ahmad al-Assal in Kitab al-Ma'rifa.

It is authentically established from him, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, with a chain of narration of Muslim, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah has angels who wander about, seeking out the gatherings of remembrance. When they find a gathering of remembrance, they sit with them. When they disperse, they ascend to their Lord." The original hadith is in the Sahih of Muslim, and its wording is: "When they disperse, they ascend to the sky. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, asks them, while He is most knowing of them, 'From where have you come?'" and the hadith continues.

Al-Daraqutni mentioned in Kitab Nuzul al-Rabb 'Azza wa Jall kulla layla ila sama' al-dunya, from the hadith of Ubada ibn al-Samit, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah descends every night to the lowest heaven when the last third of the night remains, and says: 'Is there any servant of Mine who calls upon Me, that I may answer him? Is there any wrongdoer against his own soul who calls upon Me, that I may release him?' And so it continues until the rising of dawn, and He ascends upon His Throne."

From Jabir ibn Sulaym, who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'A man among those who were before you wore two cloaks and strutted in them, so Allah looked at him from above His Throne and detested him, and He commanded the earth, and it seized him, and he will be sinking in it.'" Al-Darimi narrated it from Sahl ibn Bakkar, one of the teachers of al-Bukhari, and it has a corroborating narration in the Sahih of al-Bukhari from the hadith of Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him.

From Imran ibn Husayn, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Accept the good tidings, O Banu Tamim.' They said: 'You have given us good tidings, so give us [something].' Then some people of Yemen came in, and he said: 'Accept the good tidings, O people of Yemen, since Banu Tamim did not accept them.' They said: 'We accept. We have come to you to gain understanding of the religion, and to ask you about the beginning of this matter: what was it?' He said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, was upon the Throne, and He was before everything, and He wrote in the Preserved Tablet everything that will be.'" This is a sound hadith, its origin being in the Sahih of al-Bukhari.

Al-Khallal narrated in Kitab al-Sunna, with a sound chain of narration meeting the conditions of al-Bukhari, from Qatada ibn al-Nu'man, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "When Allah had finished creating His creation, He settled upon His Throne."

In the account of the death of the Prophet (ﷺ), from the hadith of Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him: "The Prophet (ﷺ) said to Ali, may Allah be pleased with him: 'When I die, wash me, you and Ibn Abbas, with Ibn Abbas pouring the water, and Jibril as the third of you. Shroud me in three white new garments, and place me in the mosque, for the first to pray over me will be the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, from above His Throne.'"

It has also been narrated in the hadith of Ali's proposal to Fatima, may Allah be pleased with her, that "when the Prophet (ﷺ) sought her hand in marriage, she said: 'O father, it seems you have saved me for the poor man of Quraysh.' He said: 'By the One who sent me with the truth as a prophet, I have not spoken of this until Allah gave permission for it from the sky.' She said: 'I am pleased with what Allah is pleased with for me.'"

In the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, from the hadith of Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, is the account of the intercession, the whole hadith, raised to the Prophet (ﷺ), and in it: "Then I come to my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and find Him seated upon His chair or His throne."

From Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) narrated to us: "[He] said: 'They come to me, and I walk before them until I reach the gate of Paradise. Paradise has two leaves of gold, the distance between which is five hundred years.' Ma'bad said: 'It is as if I were looking at the fingers of Anas when he opened them, saying: the distance between them is five hundred years.' Then I ask for it to be opened, and I am given permission to enter, and I enter upon my Lord and find Him sitting upon the Chair of Honor, so I fall down before Him in prostration.'" Khushaysh ibn Asram al-Nasa'i narrated it in his Kitab al-Sunna.

Abd al-Razzaq mentioned, from Ma'mar, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, "from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: 'Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, descends to the lowest heaven, and He has a chair in every heaven. When He descends to the lowest heaven, He sits upon His chair, then says: "Who is there who lends to One who is neither poor nor unjust? Who is there who seeks forgiveness from Me, that I may forgive him? Who is there who repents, that I may accept his repentance?" When it is dawn, He rises and sits upon His chair.'" Abu Abd Allah ibn Mandah narrated it. It is also narrated from Sa'id, both as a mursal and as a mawsul. Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "The mursal of Sa'id is good in our view."

From Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah gathers the creatures, He will judge them, and He will separate the people of Paradise from the people of the Fire, while He is in His Paradise upon His Throne." Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Hafiz said: "This is a sound hadith."

From Jabir ibn Sulaym, who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'A man among those before you wore two cloaks and strutted, so Allah looked at him from above His Throne, detested him, and commanded the earth, and it seized him.'" This is a sound hadith.

Abdullah ibn Bakr al-Sahmi narrated: Yazid ibn Awana narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Dhakwan, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "We were sitting one day in the courtyard of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when a woman from the daughters of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by us. A man from the people said: 'This is the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' Abu Sufyan said: 'The likeness of Muhammad among Banu Hashim is only like a basil plant in the middle of the thorny bushes.' That woman heard him and reported it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out, I think he said angry, climbed his pulpit, and said: 'What is this about statements that reach me concerning people? Indeed Allah created seven heavens and chose the highest of them and settled there, and He settled in His heavens whomever He wished of His creation. He created seven earths and chose the highest and settled in it of His creation. He chose His creation: He chose the children of Adam, then He chose the children of Adam and chose the Arabs, then He chose Mudar and chose Quraysh, then He chose Quraysh and chose Banu Hashim, then He chose Banu Hashim and chose me from Banu Hashim, so I have always been among the best. Beware, whoever loves Quraysh, it is by my love that he loves them, and whoever hates Quraysh, it is by my hatred that he hates them.'"

Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad, from the hadith of Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Ata, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, may Allah be pleased with him, from Abu (Hurayra), may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed the dying person is attended by the angels. When it is a righteous man, they say: 'Come out, O good soul, that was in a good body. Come out praised, and rejoice in rest, sweet fragrance, and a Lord not angry.' They keep saying this to it until it reaches the sky in which Allah, exalted, is. And when it is an evil man, they say: 'Come out, O wicked soul, that was in a wicked body. Come out blameworthy, and rejoice in boiling water, dark liquid, and other torments of similar kinds.' They keep saying this to it until it comes out. Then it is lifted up to the sky, and its opening is requested, and it is said: 'Who is this?' It is said: 'So-and-so.' It is said: 'No welcome to the wicked soul that was in a wicked body. Return blameworthy, for the gates of the sky will not be opened for you.' Then it is sent down from the sky and then goes to the grave..."

Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 32, verses 4–6 (part 4 of 15):

Imam Ahmad also related in his Musnad (a collection of hadith arranged by the narrators' names) from the hadith of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: "We went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for the funeral of a man from the Ansar. We reached the grave, and it had not yet been lined (with a niche). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sat down, and we sat around him as if birds were upon our heads. In his hand was a stick with which he was scratching the ground. He raised his head and said: 'Seek refuge in Allah from the punishment of the grave,' twice or three times. Then he said: 'When the believing servant is detaching from the world and turning towards the Hereafter, angels descend to him from the heaven, with white faces, as if their faces were the sun. With them is a shroud from the shrouds of Paradise and perfume from the perfumes of Paradise, until they sit at a distance as far as the eye can see. Then the Angel of Death comes and sits at his head and says: "O good soul, come out to forgiveness from Allah and good pleasure."' He said: 'It comes out and flows as a drop flows from the mouth of a waterskin. He takes it, and when he has taken it, he does not leave it in his hand for the blink of an eye. Then they take it and place it in that shroud and in that perfume, and there comes from it the finest fragrance of musk ever found on the face of the earth.' He said: 'They ascend with it, and they do not pass with it by any assembly of angels without them saying: "What is this good soul?" They reply: "So-and-so son of so-and-so," using the finest of the names by which he was called in the world, until they reach the lowest heaven and ask for it to be opened, and it is opened for them. Those nearest to God in each heaven escort it to the next heaven, until it is brought to the seventh heaven. Then Allah, exalted is He, says: "Write the record of My servant in 'Illiyyin, and return him to the earth, for I created them from it, and I will return them to it, and I will bring them out from it once more."' He said: 'His spirit is returned to his body, and two angels come to him and seat him and say to him: "Who is your Lord?" He says: "My Lord is Allah." They say: "What is your religion?" He says: "My religion is Islam." They say: "What is this man who was sent among you?" He says: "He is the Messenger of Allah." They say: "And what is your knowledge?" He says: "I recited the Book of Allah, believed in it, and affirmed it." Then a caller calls out from the heaven: "My servant has spoken the truth. Spread for him a bed from Paradise, clothe him with garments from Paradise, and open for him a door to Paradise." So there comes to him from its breeze and its fragrance, and his grave is widened for him as far as his eye can see.' He said: 'And there comes to him a man of handsome face, fine clothing and pleasant scent, who says: "Rejoice in that which will please you. This is your day which you were promised." He says to him: "Who are you? Your face is the face of one who brings good." He says: "I am your righteous deed." He says: "My Lord, establish the Hour, My Lord, establish the Hour, so that I may return to my family and my property."'"

He mentioned the hadith in full. It is sahih (authentic), and a group of the hadith memorizers (huffaz) have declared it sound.

'Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Darimi, the imam and memorizer, one of the leading imams of Islam, said: Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Hammad, who is Ibn Salama, narrated to us, 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib narrated to us, from al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When I was taken on the Night Journey, I passed by a fragrant smell. I said: 'O Jibril, what is this fragrant smell?' He said: 'This is the fragrance of the hairdresser of Pharaoh's daughter and her children. She used to comb her hair, and the comb fell from her hand, and she said: "In the name of Allah." Pharaoh's daughter said: "My father?" She said: "No, rather my Lord and the Lord of your father is Allah." She said: "I will inform my father of that." She said: "Yes." So she informed him, and he summoned her and said: "Who is your Lord? Do you have a lord other than me?" She said: "My Lord and your Lord is Allah, who is in the heaven." So he ordered a copper pot to be brought, and it was heated. Then he summoned her and her children and threw them into it.'" He related the hadith at length.

And from Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Angel of Death used to come to people visibly. He came to Musa and slapped him, and he lost his eye. So he ascended to his Lord and said: 'You sent me to Musa, and he slapped me and took my eye. Were it not for his honour before You, I would have harmed him severely.' He said: 'Return to My servant and tell him: let him place his hand on the back of a bull, and for every hair his hand covers he will have a year to live.' So he came and conveyed to him what he had been commanded. He (Musa) said: 'What comes after that?' He said: 'Death.' He said: 'Now.' So he smelled him with a smell by which he took his spirit, and Allah returned his sight to the Angel of Death." This is a sahih hadith; its origin and its corroboration are in the two Sahihs (Bukhari and Muslim).

He also said: Ibn Hisham al-Rifa'i narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated to us, from Asim ibn Bahdala, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Ibrahim was thrown into the fire, he said: 'O Allah, You are One in the heaven, and I am one on the earth, worshipping You.'"

And from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "I am amazed at two angels who descended seeking a servant at his prayer place, where he used to pray, and they did not find him. So they ascended to Allah and said: 'O our Lord, Your servant so-and-so, we used to write down his deeds for him, but we found that You have detained him in Your bonds.' He said: 'Write for My servant the deed he used to do.'" Ibn Abi al-Dunya related it, and it has a corroboration in Bukhari.

And in the hadith of Abdullah ibn Unays al-Ansari, who travelled from Madina to Egypt to Jabir ibn Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him) until he heard it from him. He said to him: "It has reached me that you narrate a hadith about the Judgment from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) which I did not witness, and no one knows it better than you." He said: "Yes. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Allah will resurrect you on the Day of Resurrection barefoot, naked, uncircumcised and without any mark. Then He will gather you, then He will call out, and He is standing upon His Throne.'" He mentioned the hadith. The imams of Ahl al-Sunna, Ahmad ibn Hanbal and others, relied on it as proof.

Al-Harith ibn Abi Usama related in his Musnad, from the hadith of Ubada ibn Nusayy, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Allah dislikes, in the heaven, that Abu Bakr be wrongly judged on the earth."

There is no contradiction between this hadith and the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying in the hadith of the dream: "You were right in part and wrong in part." This is for two reasons. The first: Allah, glorified and exalted, dislikes the correction of His Messenger by individuals of the Ummah, not the Messenger's correction of someone in some matter, for truth and correctness are certainly with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), unlike others in the Ummah. When al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) errs, he cannot be certain that correctness is with him. Rather, whenever al-Siddiq and others disputed any matter, correctness was always with al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him).

The second: the correction here refers to ascribing to him a deliberate error (al-khata' al-'amd), which is sin, as in the saying of Allah, exalted: ﴿Indeed, their killing was a great sin﴾ [al-Isra': 31], and not the error that is the opposite of knowledge. And Allah knows best.

Abu Nu'aym related from the hadith of Shu'ba, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A servant may be on the verge of one of the worldly needs, and Allah mentions him from above seven heavens and says: 'My angels, this servant of Mine has come close to one of the worldly needs. If I open it for him, I open for him a door from the doors of the Fire. But withhold it from him.' So the servant wakes up biting his fingertips, saying: 'Who has preceded me, who has humbled me?' And it was nothing but a mercy with which Allah showed mercy to him."

In the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, from the hadith of Usama ibn Zayd (may Allah be pleased with them both), he said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I do not see you fasting in any month as you fast in Sha'ban.' He said: 'That is a month which people neglect, between Rajab and Ramadan, and it is a month in which deeds are raised to the Lord of the worlds, mighty and majestic. So I love that my deed be raised while I am fasting.'"

In al-Thaqafiyyat (a collection of narrations from Thaqif, transmitted by al-Thaqafi), from the hadith of Jabir ibn Sulaym (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ): "A man from those before you wore two garments and strutted in them, so Allah looked at him from above His Throne and detested him, and He commanded the earth, and it seized him, and he continues to sink (jalajala) into the earth. So beware of the disobedience of Allah." Its origin is in the Sahih.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba said: 'Abdah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Abu Hayyan, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, that Hassan ibn Thabit (may Allah be pleased with him) recited to the Prophet (ﷺ):

I bear witness by the permission of Allah that Muhammad
Is the Messenger of the One who is above the heavens, on high.
And indeed Abu Yahya and Yahya, both of them,
Have a deed in their religion that is accepted.
And indeed the brother of al-Ahqaf, when his people are wrong,
Strives in the cause of God and does justice.

Shaykh al-Islam said: 'Ali ibn Bishr informed us, Ibn Mandah informed us, Khaythama ibn Sulayman informed us, al-Sari ibn Yahya narrated to us, Hannad ibn al-Sari narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash narrated to us, from Abu Sa'id al-Baqqal, from Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), that the Jews came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and asked him about the creation of the heavens and the earth, and he mentioned a long hadith. They said: "Then what, O Muhammad?" He said: "Then He established Himself upon the Throne." They said: "You are right, O Muhammad. If only you had completed it. Then He rested." So he became very angry, and the verse was revealed: ﴿And We created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, and no fatigue touched Us﴾ [Qaf: 38].

[Section on what has been transmitted from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the Followers, the Four Imams and others regarding this]

[The saying of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him)]

Section: On what has been transmitted from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the Followers, the Four Imams and others on this:

First: what has been transmitted from the Companions of the Messenger (ﷺ): (The saying of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him). Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba said: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from his father, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed away, Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "O people, if Muhammad was your god whom you worship, then your god has died. But if your God is Allah, who is in the heaven, then your God has not died." Then he recited: ﴿Muhammad is only a messenger; messengers have passed away before him﴾ [Al 'Imran: 144], until he finished the verse.

Al-Bukhari said in his History: Muhammad ibn Fudayl said, from Fudayl ibn Ghazwan, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed away, Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) entered upon him, bent over him, kissed his forehead and said: "May my father and mother be ransomed for you. You were good in life and in death." He said: "Whoever used to worship Muhammad, then Muhammad has died. And whoever used to worship Allah, then Allah is in the heaven, living, who does not die." In Sahih al-Bukhari, from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went to the tribe of 'Amr ibn 'Awf to reconcile between them. The prayer time came, and the muezzin came to Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) and mentioned the hadith, and in it, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gestured to Abu Bakr to remain in his place. Abu Bakr raised his hands, praised Allah for what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had commanded him, then withdrew... and he mentioned it.

[Mention of the saying of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him)]

From Isma'il, from Qays, who said: When 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) came to Syria, the people met him while he was on his camel. They said: "O Commander of the Believers, if only you would ride a horse, so that the great men and their dignitaries could meet you." 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Do I not see you here? The matter is only from here," and he gestured with his hand towards the heaven.

Abu Nu'aym also related with his chain from him: "Woe to the judge of the earth from the Judge of the heaven, on the day they meet Him, except for one who commands justice, judges with truth, does not judge by whim, kinship, desire or fear, and makes the Book of Allah a mirror before his eyes."

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 32, verse 4–6 (part 5 of 15):

ʿuthmān ibn Saʿīd al-Dārimī said: Mūsā ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim narrated to us, he said: I heard Abū Yazīd al-Muzanī say: A woman met ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may Allah be pleased with him), named Khawlah bint Thaʿlabah (may Allah be pleased with her), while he was walking with the people. She stopped him, so he stopped for her, drew near to her, and inclined his head toward her until she finished her need and departed. A man said to him: "O Commander of the Faithful, you have detained men of Quraysh for this old woman!" He said: "Woe to you! Do you know who this is?" (He said: "No.") (He said: "This is a woman whose complaint Allah heard from above the seven heavens. This is Khawlah bint Thaʿlabah. By Allah, if she had not departed from me until night, I would not have departed until she had finished her need, except that a prayer comes due, so I pray it and then return to her until she has finished her need.")

Khulayd ibn Daʿlaj narrated from Qatādah, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may Allah be pleased with him) came out of the mosque with Jārūd al-ʿAbdī. Then a woman appeared in the middle of the road, and ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) greeted her with peace. She returned his greeting and said: "Hey there, O ʿUmar! I knew you when you were called ʿUmayr in the market of ʿUkāz, herding the children with your staff. Then the days did not pass until you were called ʿUmar, and the days did not pass until you were called Commander of the Faithful. So fear Allah concerning the subjects, and know that whoever fears the threat, the distant is brought near to him, and whoever fears death, fears missing what he wants." Jārūd said: "O woman, you have spoken too much to the Commander of the Faithful!" ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Leave her. Do you not know who she is? This is Khawlah bint Ḥakīm, whose complaint Allah heard from above the seven heavens. By Allah, ʿUmar is more worthy to listen to her."

Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said: We have related from several routes that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb went out with people, and passed by an old woman who stopped him, so he stopped for her and began to speak with her while she spoke with him. A man said: "O Commander of the Faithful, you have detained the people for this old woman!" He said: "Woe to you! Do you know who this is? This is a woman whose complaint Allah heard from above the seven heavens." Then he mentioned the narration.

[The statement of ʿAbdullāh ibn Rawāḥah (may Allah be pleased with him)]

Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr (may Allah have mercy on him) said in al-Istīʿāb: We have related from sound routes that ʿAbdullāh ibn Rawāḥah (may Allah be pleased with him) went to a slave-girl of his and had intercourse with her. His wife saw him and reproached him, but he denied it. She said to him: "If you are truthful, then recite the Qur'ān, for one in a state of major ritual impurity (junub) does not recite the Qur'ān." So he said:

I bear witness that the promise of Allah is true, and that the Fire is the abode of the disbelievers.
And that the Throne floats above the water, and above the Throne is the Lord of the worlds.
And it is carried by mighty angels, the angels of Allah, marked (for their task).

She said: "I believe in Allah, and I have called my own eyes liars." She did not memorize the Qur'ān nor recite it.

[The statement of ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd (may Allah be pleased with him)]

al-Dārimī said: Mūsā ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr, from Ibn Masʿūd (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The distance between the lowest heaven and the one next to it is five hundred years, and between every two heavens is a journey of five hundred years, and between the seventh heaven and the Kursī is a journey of five hundred years, and between the Kursī and the water is a journey of five hundred years. The Throne is upon the water, and Allah, the Exalted, is above the Throne, and He knows what you are upon. al-Aʿmash narrated from Khaythamah from him: Indeed a servant may resolve upon a matter of trade or leadership, until when it is made easy for him, Allah looks at him from above the seven heavens and says to the angel: "Turn him away from it." He said: "So he turns him away."

[The statement of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both)]

ʿAbdullāh ibn Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal mentioned in the Kitāb al-Sunnah, from the hadith of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "Reflect upon everything, but do not reflect upon the Essence of Allah, for between the seven heavens and the Kursī is seven thousand light, and He is above that." In the Musnad of al-Ḥasan ibn Sufyān and the Kitāb of ʿUthmān ibn Saʿīd al-Dārimī, from the hadith of ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Mulaykah, that Dhakwān narrated to him, both said: Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with him) asked permission to enter upon ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) while she was dying. He said to her: "You were the most beloved of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ loved none but the good. Allah sent down your innocence from above the seven heavens, brought by the Trustworthy Spirit (Jibrīl). So there is no mosque of Allah's mosques in which Allah is mentioned except that it is recited therein in the hours of the night and the day."

al-Ṭabarānī mentioned in Sharḥ al-Sunnah, from the hadith of Sufyān, from Abū Hāshim, from Mujāhid, who said: It was said to Ibn ʿAbbās: "Some people deny the divine decree (qadar)." He said: "They deny the Book! If I were to seize the hair of one of them, I would pull it out. Indeed Allah was upon His Throne before He created anything. Then He created the creation and wrote what will occur until the Day of Resurrection. So people only proceed according to a matter that has already been concluded."

Isḥāq ibn Rāhawayh said: Ibrāhīm ibn al-Ḥakam ibn Abān informed us, from his father, from ʿIkrimah, concerning the words of the Exalted: ﴿Then I will surely come to them from before them and from behind them and from their right and from their left﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 17], the verse. He said: Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: "He could not say 'from above them,' because he knew that Allah is above them."

[The statement of ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her)]

(The statement of ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her.) al-Dārimī said: Mūsā ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Juwayriyah ibn Asmāʾ narrated to us, he said: I heard Nāfiʿ say: ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "By Allah, I fear that if I had wished to kill him (meaning ʿUthmān), I would have killed him. But Allah knows from above His Throne that I did not wish to kill him."

[The statement of Zaynab bint Jaḥsh, Mother of the Believers (may Allah be pleased with her)]

It is established in the two Ṣaḥīḥs, from the hadith of Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: Zaynab would boast over the wives of the Prophet ﷺ and say: "Your families gave you in marriage, but Allah married me from above the seven heavens." In another wording, related by others than the two, she used to say: "The Most Merciful married me to you from above His Throne, and Jibrīl was the envoy in that, and I am the daughter of your paternal aunt." Related by al-ʿAssāl.

[The statement of Abū Umāmah al-Bāhilī (may Allah be pleased with him)]

He said: When Allah cursed Iblīs and expelled him from His heavens and disgraced him, he said: "My Lord, You have disgraced me, cursed me, and expelled me from Your heavens and Your neighbourhood. By Your might, I will surely lead Your creation astray as long as the souls are in their bodies." The Lord, blessed and exalted, answered him, saying: "By My might, My majesty, and My loftiness above My Throne, if My servant sins until his sins fill the heaven and the earth, and then there remains of his life only one breath, and he regrets his sins, I will forgive them and replace all his evil deeds with good deeds." This wording has also been related as a marfūʿ (attributed to the Prophet ﷺ) with the wording: "By My might, My majesty, and My loftiness, if My servant..." and so on. Ibn Lahīʿah related it from Abū al-Haytham, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed Satan said: 'By Your might, O my Lord, I will not cease to lead Your servants astray as long as their souls are in their bodies.' The Lord said: 'By My might, My majesty, and the height of My station, I will not cease to forgive them so long as they seek My forgiveness.'"

[The statement of all the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them all)]

The statement of all the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them all). Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Umawī said in his Maghāzī: al-Bakkāʾī narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, who said: Yazīd ibn Sinān narrated to me, from Saʿīd ibn al-Ujayrid al-Kindī, from al-ʿUrs ibn Qays al-Kindī, from ʿAdī ibn ʿUmayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "I went out as an emigrant to the Prophet ﷺ," and he mentioned a long story, in which he said: "Then behold, he and those with him were prostrating upon their faces and claiming that their god is in the sky. So I embraced Islam and followed him."

[Mention of the statements of the Successors (may Allah have mercy on them)]

The statement of Masrūq (may Allah have mercy on him): ʿAlī ibn al-Aqmar said: When Masrūq narrated from ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her), he would say: "The truthful one (al-Ṣiddīqah), daughter of the Truthful one (al-Ṣiddīq), beloved of the Beloved of Allah ﷺ, the one declared innocent from above the seven heavens, told me..."

[The statement of ʿIkrimah (may Allah have mercy on him)]

Salamah ibn Shabīb said: Ibrāhīm ibn al-Ḥakam narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to me, from ʿIkrimah (may Allah have mercy on him), who said: While a man was reclining on his back in Paradise, he said to himself, without moving his lips: "If only Allah would permit me, I would sow in Paradise." He had not finished when the angels at the gates of his Paradise, holding their palms, said: "Peace be upon you." He sat upright, and they said to him: "Your Lord says to you: You wished for something within yourself. We know it, and He has sent this seed with us. He says to you: Sow." So he cast it to the right and left, before him and behind him, and there sprouted up like mountains, according to what he wished and more. Then the Lord said to him from above His Throne: "Eat, O son of Adam, for the son of Adam is never satisfied."

[The statement of Qatādah (may Allah have mercy on him)]

al-Dārimī said: Mūsā ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Abū Hilāl narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to us, who said: The Children of Israel said: "O Lord, You are in the heaven and we are on the earth, so how can we know Your pleasure and Your anger?" He said: "When I am pleased with you, I appoint over you your best, and when I am angry with you, I appoint over you your worst."

[The statement of Sulaymān al-Taymī (may Allah have mercy on him)]

Ibn Abī Khaythamah said in his Tārīkh: Hārūn ibn Maʿrūf narrated to us, he said: Ḍamrah narrated to us, from Ṣadaqah al-Taymī, from Sulaymān al-Taymī, who said: "If I were asked, 'Where is Allah?' I would say: 'In the heaven.'"
