[The statement of Kaʿb al-Aḥbār (may Allah have mercy on him)]

al-Layth ibn Saʿd said: Khālid ibn Yazīd narrated to me, from Saʿīd ibn Abī Hilāl, that Zayd ibn Aslam narrated to him, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, who said: A man came to Kaʿb while he was among a group and said: "O Abū Isḥāq, tell me about al-Jabbār." The people magnified his words, but Kaʿb said: "Leave the man. If he is ignorant, he will learn, and if he is knowledgeable, he will increase in knowledge." Then Kaʿb said: "I inform you that Allah created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them, then made the distance between every two heavens like the distance between the lowest heaven and the earth, and thickened them to the same degree. Then He raised the Throne and istawā (rose over) it."

Nuʿaym ibn Ḥammād said: Abū Ṣafwān al-Umawī informed us, from Yūnus ibn Yazīd, from al-Zuhrī, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, from Kaʿb, who said: Allah said in the Torah: "I am Allah, above My servants, and My Throne is above all My creation, and I am upon My Throne, governing the affairs of My servants. Nothing of the affairs of My servants is hidden from Me, in My heaven or on My earth, and to Me is the return of My creation. I inform them of what was hidden from them of My knowledge. I forgive whom I will of them by My forgiveness, and I punish whom I will by My punishment."

[The statement of Muqātil (may Allah have mercy on him)]

al-Bayhaqī mentioned in al-Asmāʾ wa al-Ṣifāt, from Bakr ibn Maʿrūf, from Muqātil: "It has reached us, and Allah knows best, concerning the words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿He is the First and the Last, and the Apparent and the Hidden﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 3], the verse: 'The First' is before everything, 'the Last' is after everything, 'the Apparent' is above everything, and 'the Hidden' is nearer to everything than anything. He means nearness by His knowledge and power, while He is above His Throne, and He is with everything in knowledge." By this same chain from him, concerning the words of the Exalted: ﴿He is with them wherever they are﴾ [al-Mujādilah: 7], he said: "He means by His knowledge, and that is His saying: ﴿Indeed Allah is Knowing of all things﴾ [al-Anfāl: 75]. So He knows their secret conversation and hears their speech, then He will inform them on the Day of Resurrection of everything, while He is above His Throne and His knowledge is with them."

[The statement of al-Ḍaḥḥāk (may Allah have mercy on him)]

Bukayr ibn Maʿrūf narrated from Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān, from him (al-Ḍaḥḥāk), concerning ﴿There is no secret conference of three but He is their fourth, nor of five but He is their sixth...﴾ [al-Mujādilah: 7], the verse. He said: "He is Allah upon the Throne, and His knowledge is with them."

[The statement of the Successors collectively]

Ibn al-Qayyim's commentary on Surah 32, verses 4–6 (part 6 of 15):

Al-Bayhaqi narrated with a sound chain (isnad) from al-Awza'i, who said: "We and the Followers (al-Tabi'un) were in great numbers, and we used to say: Indeed Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, is above His Throne, and we affirm what the Sunnah (the prophetic tradition) has reported of His attributes." Shaykh al-Islam said: "Al-Awza'i only said this after the emergence of Jahm (Jahm ibn Safwan, the founder of the Jahmiyya), who denied that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is above His Throne and who negated His attributes, so that people would know that the way of the Salaf (the early pious predecessors) was contrary to his view."

Abu Umar Ibn Abd al-Barr said in al-Tamhid: "Because the scholars among the Companions and the Followers, from whom interpretation (ta'wil) was transmitted, said concerning the interpretation of Allah's words: ﴿There is no secret conversation between three but that He is the fourth of them, nor between five but that He is the sixth of them﴾ [al-Mujadila: 7]: He is above the Throne, and His knowledge is in every place. No one opposed them in this, and his statement is not to be relied upon as an argument."

[The saying of al-Hasan, may Allah have mercy on him]

Abu Bakr al-Hudhali narrated from al-Hasan, may Allah have mercy on him, that he said: "Nothing among creation is closer to your Lord than Israfil. Between him and his Lord are seven veils, each veil a distance of five hundred years. Israfil is below these, his head is beneath the Throne and his feet are in the depths of the earth (al-Thara)."

[The saying of Malik ibn Dinar, may Allah have mercy on him]

Abu al-Abbas al-Sarraj mentioned: Abdullah ibn Abi Ziyad and Harun narrated to us, both saying: Sayyar narrated to us, [he] said: Ja'far narrated to us, saying: I heard Malik ibn Dinar say: "Indeed the sincere (al-Siddiqun) when the Qur'an is recited to them, their hearts yearn for the Hereafter. Then he would say: 'Listen,' and it would be recited, and he would say: 'Listen to His truthful word from above His Throne.'" Malik ibn Dinar and others among the Salaf used to mention this report: "Son of Adam, My good comes down to you, and your evil ascends to Me. I show you love through blessings, and you show hatred to Me through sins. A noble angel does not cease to ascend to Me with an evil deed from you."

[The saying of Rabi'a ibn Abi Abd al-Rahman, may Allah have mercy on him, the teacher of Malik ibn Anas, may Allah's mercy be upon him]

Yahya ibn Adam narrated from his father, from Ibn Uyayna, who said: Rabi'a was asked about the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿The Most Merciful is established upon the Throne﴾ [Ta-Ha: 5]: "How is He established?" He said: "Istiwa' (establishment) is not unknown, the how (al-kayf) is not conceivable, from Allah is the message, upon the Messenger (ﷺ) is the conveying, and upon us is the affirmation (al-tasdiq)."

[The saying of Abdullah ibn al-Kawwa, may Allah have mercy on him]

The memorizer (al-Hafiz) Abu al-Qasim Ibn Asakir, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned in his History, from Hisham ibn Sa'd, who said: Abdullah ibn al-Kawwa came to Mu'awiya, and he said to him: "Inform me about the people of Basra." He said: "They fight together and retreat divided." He said: "Inform me about the people of Kufa." He said: "The most watchful of people over a small matter and the most prone to fall into a major one." He said: "Inform me about the people of Medina." He said: "The most eager of people for strife and the least capable of it." He said: "Inform me about the people of Egypt." He said: "A morsel of food." He said: "Inform me about the people of al-Jazira." He said: "A patch of dirt between two cities." He said: "Inform me about the people of Mosul." He said: "A necklace of a slave-girl, in which there is a bead of everything." He said: "Inform me about the people of Syria." He said: "The soldiers of the Commander of the Faithful; I will say nothing about them." He said: "You must say it." He said: "The most obedient of people to a creature, and the most disobedient to the Creator, and they do not reckon the sky to have an inhabitant."

[The saying of the Followers of the Followers collectively, may Allah have mercy on them]

[Mention of the saying of Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, may Allah have mercy on him]

Al-Darimi, al-Hakim, al-Bayhaqi and others narrated with a most authentic chain to Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak say: "We know our Lord by [the fact] that He is above the seven heavens, established upon the Throne, separate from His creation, and we do not say as the Jahmiyya say." In another wording: I said: "How do we know our Lord?" He said: "In the seventh heaven, upon His Throne, and we do not say as the Jahmiyya say."

Al-Darimi said: al-Hasan ibn al-Sabbah al-Bazzar narrated to us, [he said]: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq narrated to us from Ibn al-Mubarak, who said: It was said to him: "How do we know our Lord?" He said: "That He is above the seventh heaven, upon the Throne, separate from His creation." The Imam Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Darimi said: "Among what confirms the saying of Ibn al-Mubarak is the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to the slave-girl: 'Where is Allah?' He was testing thereby her faith. When she said: 'In the heaven,' he said: 'Free her, for she is a believer.' The reports on this from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) are numerous, the proofs are mutually reinforcing, and praise be to Allah for that." Then al-Darimi, may Allah have mercy on him, went on to cite them.

Ibn Khuzayma mentioned from Ibn al-Mubarak that a man said to him: "O Abu Abd al-Rahman, I have feared from the abundance of my supplication against the Jahmiyya." He said: "Do not fear, for they claim that your God who is in the heaven is nothing." It is authentically reported from Ibn al-Mubarak that he said: "We are able to relate the speech of the Jews and Christians, but we are not able to relate the speech of the Jahmiyya."

[The saying of al-Awza'i, may Allah have mercy on him]

Abu Abd Allah al-Hakim said: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Jawhari in Baghdad informed me, [he said]: Ibrahim ibn al-Haytham narrated to us, [he said]: Muhammad ibn Kathir al-Misisi narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Awza'i say: "We and the Followers were in great numbers, saying: Indeed Allah, His remembrance is exalted, is above His Throne, and we affirm what the Sunnah has reported." This report falls within the account of his school and the schools of the Followers, therefore we have mentioned it in both places.

[The saying of Hammad ibn Zayd, may Allah have mercy on him]

The Imam of Imams, Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Khuzayma, said: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, [he said]: Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us, [he said]: I heard Hammad ibn Zayd say: "The Jahmiyya are only trying to say: There is nothing in the heaven." Shaykh al-Islam said: "What the Jahmiyya were trying to do has been openly declared by their later ones. The prevalence of the Sunnah and the multitude of Imams in the time of those [earlier Imams] stood between them and openly declaring it. But when the era grew distant, the Sunnah became obscure and the Imams passed away, the negating Jahmiyya openly declared what their predecessors had been trying to say and could not manifest."

[The saying of Sufyan al-Thawri]

Ma'dan said: I asked Sufyan al-Thawri about the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And He is with you wherever you are﴾ [al-Hadid: 4]. He said: "[It is] His knowledge." Abu Umar mentioned it.

[The saying of Wahb ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him]

Al-Athram said: Abu Abd Allah al-Ausi narrated to us, [he said]: I heard Wahb ibn Jarir say: "The Jahmiyya only mean that there is nothing in the heaven." He said: And I said to Sulayman ibn Harb: "What did Hammad ibn Zayd used to say about the Jahmiyya?" He said: "He used to say: They only mean that there is nothing in the heaven."

[Mention of the sayings of the four Imams, may Allah have mercy on them]

[The saying of the Imam Abu Hanifa, may Allah sanctify his soul]

Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Bakr ibn al-Harith al-Faqih narrated to us, [he said]: Abu Muhammad ibn Hayyan informed us, [he said]: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Nasr narrated to us, [he said]: Yahya ibn Ya'la narrated to us, [he said]: I heard Nu'aym ibn Hammad say: I heard Nuh ibn Abi Maryam, Abu Isma, say: "We were with Abu Hanifa when [this matter] first appeared, when a woman from Tirmidh came to him, who had been sitting with Jahm. She entered Kufa, and it was said to her: 'Here is a man who has reflected upon rational matters, called Abu Hanifa, so go to him.' She came to him and said: 'Are you the one who teaches people questions, and you have abandoned your religion? Where is your God whom you worship?' He was silent before her, then remained for seven days without answering her. Then he came out to us, having written a book: 'Indeed Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, is in the heaven, not in the earth.' A man said to him: 'What do you say about the words of Allah: ﴿And He is with you﴾ [al-Hadid: 4]?' He said: 'It is as when you write to a man: I am with you, while you are absent from him.'"

Al-Bayhaqi said: "Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, was right in what he negated from Allah, exalted and sanctified above being in the earth, and in what he mentioned of the interpretation of the verse, and he followed the unrestricted text (mutlaq al-sam') in his saying that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is in the heaven."

Shaykh al-Islam said: In the book al-Fiqh al-Akbar (the Greater Jurisprudence), well known among the companions of Abu Hanifa, which they transmitted with a chain from Abu Mut'i al-Balkhi, al-Hakam ibn Abd Allah, who said: "I asked Abu Hanifa about al-Fiqh al-Akbar, and he said: Do not declare anyone a disbeliever for a sin, do not deny anyone faith, command the good and forbid the evil, know that what has befallen you was not going to miss you, and what has missed you was not going to befall you, do not disassociate from any of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), do not show loyalty to one over another, and refer the matter of Uthman and Ali, may Allah be pleased with them both, to Allah, the Exalted."

Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "The Greater Jurisprudence in religion is better than jurisprudence in knowledge, and that a man should understand how to worship his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, is better than gathering much knowledge." Abu Mut'i said: "I said: Then inform me about the best jurisprudence?" He said: "That a man learns faith, the laws, the Sunnahs, the prescribed punishments, and the disagreement of the Imams." He mentioned questions on faith, then he mentioned questions on destiny (al-qadar)... Then he said: "I said: What do you say about one who commands the good and forbids the evil, and some people follow him in that, so he departs from the community (al-jama'a)? Do you approve of that?" He said: "No." I said: "Why? Allah has commanded His Messenger (ﷺ), may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, to command the good and forbid the evil, and it is an obligatory duty." He said: "That is so, but they cause more corruption than they do good, through shedding blood and making the forbidden permissible." He mentioned discussion on fighting the Kharijites and the rebels (al-bughat), until he said: Abu Hanifa said: "Whoever says: I do not know whether my Lord is in the heaven or in the earth, has disbelieved, because Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿The Most Merciful is established upon the Throne﴾ [Ta-Ha: 5], and His Throne is above the seven heavens." (I said): "If he says: He is established upon the Throne, but he says: I do not know whether the Throne is in the heaven or in the earth?" He said: "He is a disbeliever, because he denied that [Allah] is in the heaven, since He, the Exalted, is in the highest 'Illiyyin, and He is called upon from above, not from below." In another wording: "I asked Abu Hanifa about one who says: I do not know whether my Lord is in the heaven or in the earth. He said: He has disbelieved, because Allah says: ﴿The Most Merciful is established upon the Throne﴾ [Ta-Ha: 5], and His Throne is above the seven heavens." He said: "He says: He is established upon the Throne, but he does not know whether the Throne is in the earth or in the heaven." He said: "If he denies that He is in the heaven, he has disbelieved."

Ibn al-Qayyim's *Tafsir* (part 7 of 15), on Surah 32, verses 4–6:

This was also narrated from the Shaykh al-Islam Abu Isma'il al-Ansari in his book *al-Faruq*, through his isnad (chain of narration).

Shaykh al-Islam Abu'l-Abbas, may Allah have mercy on him, said: In this famous statement of Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, as transmitted by his companions, he declared disbelief in the agnostic who says, "I do not know whether my Lord is in the heaven or in the earth." How then would the denier who says, "He is neither in the heaven nor in the earth," not be a disbeliever? Abu Hanifa based his judgment of disbelief on the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿The Most Merciful is established upon the Throne﴾ [Ta-Ha: 5]. He said: "And His Throne is above the seven heavens." Through this he showed that the Exalted's words, ﴿The Most Merciful is established upon the Throne﴾ [Ta-Ha: 5], indicate that Allah is above the heavens, above the Throne, and that establishment upon the Throne indicates that Allah Himself, in His essence, is above the Throne. He then followed this with the disbelief of one who says that He is established upon the Throne but hesitates over whether the Throne is in the heaven or in the earth. He said: "Because he denied that He is in the heaven, and that Allah is in the highest of the 'Illiyyun, and that He is called upon from above and not from below." He argued that Allah is in the highest of the 'Illiyyun and that He is called upon from above and not from below. Each of these two arguments is innate and rational, for hearts are naturally inclined to affirm that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is on high, and that He is called upon from above and not from below. Likewise were his companions after him, such as Abu Yusuf and Hisham ibn 'Ubayd Allah al-Razi, as Ibn Abi Hatim and Shaykh al-Islam transmitted with their chains of narration, that Hisham ibn 'Ubayd Allah al-Razi, companion of Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, judge of al-Rayy, imprisoned a man for Tajahhum (the Jahmite doctrine). The man repented, so he was brought to Hisham to be tested. He said, "Praise be to Allah for repentance." Hisham tested him, saying: "Do you testify that Allah is upon His Throne, separate from His creation?" He replied: "I testify that Allah is upon His Throne, but I do not know what 'separate from His creation' means." Hisham said: "Return him to prison, for he has not repented." The statement of al-Tahawi will come later, in the section on the statements of the people of hadith.

[The statement of the Imam of the Abode of Migration (Dar al-Hijra), Malik ibn Anas, may Allah have mercy on him]

Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr mentioned in his book *al-Tamhid*: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Mu'min informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan ibn Malik narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated to us (saying): my father narrated to me (saying): Shurayh ibn al-Nu'man narrated to us (saying): 'Abd Allah ibn Nafi' narrated to us, saying: Malik ibn Anas said: "Allah is in the heaven, and His knowledge is in every place, (no place is empty of it)." He said: It was said to Malik: "The Most Merciful is established upon the Throne" [Ta-Ha: 5]. How is He established? Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "Establishment is known, its modality is unknown, asking about this is an innovation, and I see you as an evil man." Likewise were the leading scholars among the companions of Malik after him.

[The statement of the leading scholars among the companions of Malik after him]

Yahya ibn Ibrahim al-Tulaytuli said in his book *Siyar al-Fuqaha*, which is a grand book rich in knowledge: 'Abd al-Malik ibn Habib narrated to me, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughira, from al-Thawri, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, who said: "They disliked a man saying, 'Alas for the times (ya khaybat al-dahr),' for they said, 'Allah is the Time (al-Dahr).' They disliked a man saying, 'May my nose be rubbed in the dust for Allah (rugham anfi lillah),' for only the nose of the disbeliever is rubbed in the dust. They disliked a man saying, 'No, by Him whose seal is upon my mouth,' for only the mouth of the disbeliever is sealed. They disliked a man saying, 'By Allah, wherever He is,' or 'Allah is in every place.'" Asbagh said: "He is established upon His Throne, and His knowledge and encompassing is in every place." Asbagh is among the most distinguished and most learned of Malik's companions.

[Mention of the statement of Abu 'Amr al-Talamankî]

He said in his book on the fundamentals (*al-Usul*): "The Muslims of the People of the Sunnah have unanimously agreed that Allah is established upon His Throne in His essence." He also said in this same book: "The People of the Sunnah have unanimously agreed that Allah, the Exalted, is established upon the Throne in its true meaning, not in a figurative sense." He then cited with his chain, from Malik, his words: "Allah is in the heaven, and His knowledge is in every place." Then he said in this book: "The Muslims of the People of the Sunnah have unanimously agreed that the meaning of the Exalted's words, ﴿And He is with you wherever you are﴾ [al-Hadid: 4], and similar verses of the Qur'an, is that this refers to His knowledge, while Allah is above the heavens, in His essence, established upon His Throne as He wills." These are his words in his book.

[Mention of the statement of the Bukhari of the West, the Imam and memorizer Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr, Imam of the Sunnah in his time, may Allah have mercy on him]

He said in *al-Tamhid*, in explaining the eighth hadith of Ibn Shihab, from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, who said: "Our Lord descends every night to the lowest heaven when the last third of the night remains, and says: 'Who will call upon Me that I may answer him? Who will ask of Me that I may give him? Who will seek My forgiveness that I may forgive him?'" This hadith is established in transmission, with a sound chain, and the people of hadith do not differ over its authenticity. In it is evidence that Allah, Exalted is He, is in the heaven upon the Throne, above the seven heavens, as the majority have said. This is their proof against the Mu'tazila and the Jahmiyya in their claim that Allah is in every place and not upon the Throne. The evidence for the correctness of what the people of truth say on this matter is the Exalted's words: ﴿The Most Merciful is established upon the Throne﴾ [Ta-Ha: 5]; and His words: ﴿Then He established Himself upon the Throne; you have not, besides Him, any protector or intercessor. Will you not then remember?﴾ [al-Sajda: 4]; and His words: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke﴾ [Fussilat: 11]; and His words: ﴿Surely they would have sought a way to the Owner of the Throne﴾ [al-Isra': 42]; and the words of Him whose name is blessed: ﴿To Him ascend the good words, and righteous deed raises them﴾ [Fatir: 10]; and His words: ﴿So when His Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble﴾ [al-A'raf: 143]; and His words: ﴿Are you secure from He who is in the heaven, that He will cause the earth to swallow you?﴾ [al-Mulk: 16]; and He said: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ [al-A'la: 1]. This is from elevation. Likewise His words: ﴿the Most High, the Magnificent﴾ [al-Baqara: 255]; and ﴿the Great, the Exalted﴾ [al-Ra'd: 9]; and ﴿Raised in degrees, Possessor of the Throne﴾ [Ghafir: 15]; and ﴿They fear their Lord above them﴾ [al-Nahl: 50]. The Jahmi says that He is below. He, may His remembrance be exalted, said: ﴿He arranges the affair from the heaven to the earth; then it ascends to Him﴾ [al-Sajda: 5]. He said to 'Isa: ﴿I will cause you to die and raise you to Me﴾ [Al 'Imran: 55]; and He said: ﴿Rather, Allah raised him to Himself﴾ [al-Nisa': 158]; and He said: ﴿Those who are near your Lord glorify Him﴾ [Fussilat: 38]; and He said: ﴿There is no repeller of it from Allah, Owner of the ascending stairways. The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 2–4]. Ascent is rising upward. As for His words: ﴿Are you secure from He who is in the heaven﴾ [al-Mulk: 16], its meaning is "He who is above the heaven," meaning upon the Throne. The preposition *fi* (in) may mean *'ala* (upon), as you see in His words: ﴿So travel in the earth﴾ [al-Tawba: 2], meaning upon the earth; and likewise His words: ﴿And I will surely crucify you upon the trunks of palm trees﴾ [Ta-Ha: 71]. All of this is reinforced by His words: ﴿The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 4]. And whatever is like it among the verses we have recited on this subject. All these verses are clear in refuting the statement of the Mu'tazila. As for their claim of figurative meaning in *istawa* (established), and their interpretation of *istawa* as *istawla* (seized dominion), there is no meaning to this, for it is not apparent in the language, and the meaning of *istila'* (seizing) in the language is overpowering, while Allah, the Exalted, is not overpowered, and no one is above Him, for He is the One, the Eternal Refuge.

It is required that speech be taken in its literal sense, unless the community agrees that a figurative sense is intended, for there is no way to follow what has been sent down to us from our Lord, the Exalted, except in this manner. The words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, are understood according to their most well-known and apparent aspects, so long as nothing requires otherwise that must be accepted. If claiming figurative meaning were permitted for every claimant, no act of worship would be established. Allah is exalted above addressing us except in what the Arabs understand from their customary forms of address, in a way whose meaning is clear to the listeners. *Istiwa'* (establishment) is known and understood in the language, and it means: height and elevation over a thing, settling and being firmly placed in it. Abu 'Ubayda said regarding the words ﴿The Most Merciful is established upon the Throne﴾ [Ta-Ha: 5]: "He rose high." He said: The Arabs say, "I *istawaytu* (ascended) upon the beast," and "I *istawaytu* upon the house." Others said: *istawa* means *istaqarra* (settled), and they cited the words of the Exalted: ﴿And when he reached his maturity and was fully grown (istawa)﴾ [al-Qasas: 14], meaning his youth reached its completion and settled, so that there was no further increase in his youth. Ibn 'Abd al-Barr said: *Istiwa'* is settling in elevation, and with this Allah addressed us in His Book, saying: ﴿That you may sit firmly upon its back, then remember the favor of your Lord when you are seated upon it﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 13]; and He said: ﴿And it rested (istawat) upon al-Judi﴾ [Hud: 44]; and He said: ﴿And when you are seated (istawayta), you and those with you, upon the ship﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 28].

The poet said:
"You brought them to water in a barren desert wasteland, / when the Yemeni star had risen and settled (istawa)."

This cannot be interpreted by anyone as *istawla* (seized), for a star does not seize dominion. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl, who was trustworthy, reliable, and distinguished in the knowledge of religion and language, mentioned: "Al-Khalil narrated to me, and sufficient for you is al-Khalil, who said: I came to Abu Rabi'a al-A'rabi, who was among the most knowledgeable people I had seen. He was on a roof. We greeted him, and he returned our greeting and said to us: 'Istawu (ascend/be level).' We remained bewildered and did not know what he said. A Bedouin beside him said to us: 'He has commanded you to rise up.' Al-Khalil said: It is from the words of Allah: ﴿Then He turned (istawa) to the heaven while it was smoke﴾ [Fussilat: 11]. So we climbed up to him."

As for the objection of those who drew from among them a hadith narrated by 'Abd Allah ibn Dawud al-Wasiti, from Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Samad, from 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Mujahid, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, regarding the words of the Exalted: ﴿The Most Merciful is established upon the Throne﴾ [Ta-Ha: 5], that he said: "He seized dominion over all His creation, so no place is empty of Him." The response is: this hadith is munkar (rejected) as attributed to Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, and its transmitters are unknown or weak. As for 'Abd Allah ibn Dawud al-Wasiti and 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Mujahid, both are weak; and Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Samad is unknown and not recognized. And they (the Mu'tazila and Jahmiyya) do not accept the reports of reliable individual narrators (ahad). How then could it be lawful for them to argue with such a hadith, if they had understanding and were fair? Have they not heard Allah, Glorified is He, saying: ﴿And Pharaoh said: O Haman, build for me a tower that I may reach the ways, the ways of the heavens, and look at the God of Moses; but indeed, I think him a liar﴾ [Ghafir: 36–37]. This shows that Moses, upon him be blessings and peace, used to say that his God is in the heaven, and Pharaoh thought him a liar.

The poet said:
"Glory be to Him whom creation does not appraise at His true measure, / and who is above the Throne, the One, the Unique."
"Sovereign upon the Throne of the heaven, the Guardian, / before His might the faces humble themselves and prostrate."

These verses belong to Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt, and in them he says, describing the angels:
"And those who prostrate to Him do not raise their heads for ages, / glorifying a Lord who is above them and exalting Him."

He said: If they argue with His saying, ﴿And He is the One who is God in the heavens and God on the earth﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 84], and with His saying, ﴿And He is Allah in the heavens and in the earth﴾ [al-An'am: 3], and with His saying, ﴿There is no secret conversation between three but that He is their fourth, nor between five but that He is their sixth﴾ [al-Mujadila: 7], and they claim that Allah, glorified is He, is in every place by His essence and His being, blessed and exalted is His majesty, it is said to them: There is no disagreement between us, you, and the rest of the Ummah that He is not in the earth beneath the heaven by His essence. Therefore these verses must be understood according to the correct meaning on which there is consensus. That meaning is that He is a deity worshipped by the people of the heavens, in the heavens, and a deity worshipped by the people of the earth, on the earth. This is also what the scholars of tafsir (Qur'anic exegesis) have said. The apparent sense of the revelation testifies that He is over the Throne, so the disagreement on this is baseless, and the happiest of people with it is the one whom the apparent meaning supports. As for His saying in the other verse, ﴿and on the earth a God﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 84], consensus and agreement have made clear that the meaning is that He is worshipped by the people of the earth. So reflect on this, for it is decisive.

Among the proofs also that He, Mighty and Majestic, is over the Throne above the seven heavens is that all the monotheists, Arab and non-Arab, when a matter distresses them or a hardship befalls them, raise their faces to the sky and lift their hands, pointing with them toward the sky, calling upon Allah their Lord, blessed and exalted. This is more famous and better known among the elite and the common folk than that it needs to be supported by much narration, because it is an involuntary act that no one imposed upon them, nor did any Muslim deny it to them. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to the slave-girl whose master wanted to free her, "If she is a believer." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) tested her by saying to her, "Where is Allah?" She pointed to the sky. Then he said to her, "Who am I?" She said, "You are the Messenger of Allah." He said, "Free her, for she is a believer." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was satisfied from her with her raising her head toward the sky, and was content with that alone, without anything else.

As for their argument with His saying, ﴿There is no secret conversation between three but that He is their fourth﴾ [al-Mujadila: 7], there is no proof for them in the apparent meaning of this verse, because the scholars among the Companions and the Successors (tabi'un), from whom interpretation of the Qur'an was transmitted, said in its interpretation: He is over the Throne, and His knowledge is in every place. No one who opposed them in this has been cited as a source whose words can be used as proof. Sunayd mentioned from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, regarding His saying, ﴿There is no secret conversation between three but that He is their fourth﴾, that he said: He is over His Throne, and His knowledge is with them wherever they are. He said: And it has reached me from Sufyan al-Thawri something similar.

Sunayd said: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us from Asim ibn Bahdala, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Allah is above the Throne; nothing of your deeds is hidden from Him. Then he cited through the route of Yazid ibn Harun, from Hammad ibn Salama, from Asim ibn Bahdala, from Zirr, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The distance between the heaven and the earth is a five-hundred-year journey, and the distance between each heaven and the next is a five-hundred-year journey, and the distance between the seventh heaven and the Kursi is a five-hundred-year journey, and the distance between the Kursi and the water is a five-hundred-year journey. The Throne is upon the water, and Allah is upon the Throne, and He knows your deeds. He mentioned this statement, or something close to it, in the book al-Istidhkar.

[The statement of the Imam Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Isa al-Maliki, well known as Ibn Abi Zamanin, may Allah have mercy on him]

He said in his book which he composed on the foundations of the Sunnah: Chapter on belief in the Throne. He said: Among the statements of the People of the Sunnah is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the Throne and singled it out for loftiness and elevation above all that He created, then He istawa (established Himself) upon it as He wills, as He informed about Himself in His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿The Most Merciful is established upon the Throne﴾ [Ta-Ha: 5], and in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then He established Himself upon the Throne. He knows what enters into the earth and what emerges from it, and what descends from the heaven and what ascends therein﴾ [al-Hadid: 4]. He mentioned the hadith of Abu Razin al-Uqayli, who said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, where was our Lord before He created the heavens and the earth?" He said: "He was in 'ama' (a cloud), with nothing above it and nothing below it. Then He created His Throne upon the water." Then he mentioned the narrations on this, until he said: Chapter on belief in the veils. He said: Among the statements of the People of the Sunnah is that Allah, Exalted is He, is distinct from His creation, veiled from them by veils, exalted is Allah above what the wrongdoers say, a great exaltation: ﴿How great a word it is that comes out of their mouths; they say nothing but a lie﴾ [al-Kahf: 5]. Until he said: Chapter on belief in the descent. He said: Among the statements of the People of the Sunnah is that Allah descends to the lowest heaven, and he mentioned the hadith of the descent. Then he said: This hadith makes clear that Allah, Exalted is He, is over His Throne in the heaven, not in the earth. This is also clear in the Book of Allah, Exalted and Sanctified, and in more than one hadith from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿He manages the affair from the heaven to the earth﴾ [al-Sajda: 5], ﴿then it ascends to Him﴾ [al-Sajda: 5]. He cited verses on elevation, and he mentioned through the route of Anas ibn Malik the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) to the slave-girl, "Where is Allah?" Then he said: Hadiths like this are very numerous.

[Mention of the statement of the Imam Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, sanctify his spirit, and illuminate his tomb]

The Imam Ibn al-Imam Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatim al-Razi said: Abu Shu'ayb and Abu Thawr narrated to us from Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, who said: The position on the Sunnah upon which I am, and upon which I saw our companions, the people of hadith whom I saw and from whom I took, such as Sufyan and Malik and others, is: affirming the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and that Allah is over His Throne in His heaven, near to His creation as He wills, and that Allah descends to the lowest heaven as He wills. Abd al-Rahman said: Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i say, when he was asked about the attributes of Allah and what one should believe concerning them: Allah, Exalted is He, has names and attributes which His Book brought and which His Prophet informed his Ummah about. No one among the creation of Allah for whom the proof has been established may reject them, because the Qur'an came with them, and the statement of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) regarding them was authentically reported by trustworthy narrators. If someone opposes this after the proof has been established against him, he is a disbeliever. But before the proof is established against him, he is excused by ignorance, because knowledge of this is not attained by reason, nor by thought and the heart. We do not declare anyone a disbeliever for ignorance of them until the report has reached him and these attributes have been confirmed to him. We affirm these attributes and negate tashbih (anthropomorphism) from them, as He negated tashbih from Himself, when He said: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾ [al-Shura: 11]. It is authentically reported from al-Shafi'i that he said: The caliphate of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, is true; Allah decreed it in His heaven and brought together upon it the hearts of the Companions of His Prophet. It is known that what is decreed on the earth, and the decree is His act, Glorified and Exalted is He, includes His will and His power. He also said in the introduction to his Risala: "All praise is due to Allah, who is as He described Himself and beyond what His creation describes Him." Thus he made His attributes, Glorified is He, only to be received through revelation (sam'). Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la said: Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, said to me: The foundation is the Qur'an and the Sunnah; if there is none, then analogy based on these two. When a hadith is connected to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and its chain is authentic, it is Sunnah. Consensus (ijma') is greater than an isolated report (khabar mufrad). The hadith is taken according to its apparent meaning; and when it admits of several meanings, the one most resembling its apparent meaning is the more fitting. Al-Khatib said in al-Kifaya: Abu Nu'aym al-Hafiz informed us, Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Hayyan narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, Abu Hatim al-Razi narrated to us, Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, and he mentioned it with this text.

[The statement of his companion, the leading Shafi'i scholar of his time, Abu Ibrahim Isma'il ibn Yahya al-Muzani]

In his Risala on the Sunnah, which al-Silafi, Abu Tahir, narrated from him with his chain, and we cite it in full with its wording: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. May Allah protect us and you with taqwa (God-consciousness), and grant us and you success in agreeing with guidance. To proceed: You asked me to clarify for you a matter of the Sunnah by which you may guide yourself to hold fast to it, and by which you may ward off from yourself the confusion of doubtful sayings and the deviation of the innovations of the misguided. I have set out for you a clear path, and I have not spared myself or you in sincere advice in it. I began it with praise of Allah, Lord of right guidance and direction. All praise belongs to Allah, the most worthy of being begun with, the most deserving of being thanked and praised, the One, the Self-Sufficient, who has no consort and no son, exalted above likeness, having no equal and no peer, the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing, the All-Knowing, the All-Aware, the Impregnable, the Exalted in rank. He is high above His Throne, yet near by His knowledge to His creation. His knowledge encompasses affairs and His pre-eternal decree is executed in His creation. ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal﴾. The creatures act according to His prior knowledge and proceed toward what He created for them of good and evil. They possess nothing of obedience for themselves, and they find no way to turn away disobedience from themselves. He created the creation by His will without any need for it. He created all the angels for His obedience and disposed them to His worship. Among them are angels who by His power carry the Throne, and a group around His Throne glorifying Him, and others praising Him and sanctifying Him. He chose from among them messengers to His messengers, and some of them manage His affairs. Then He created Adam with His hand, and made him dwell in His Garden. Before that He had created him for the earth, and forbade him a tree upon which His decree had already been executed that he would eat from it. Then He tested him with what He had forbidden him from it. Then He set his enemy over him, and he misled him into it, and made his eating it the cause of his descent to the earth. He found no way to abandon eating it and no path to avoid it. Then He created for the Garden from his offspring people, and they, by their deeds, act by His will, and by His power and His desire they carry out. And from his offspring He created people for the Fire. He created for them eyes with which they do not see, ears with which they do not hear, and hearts with which they do not understand. They are thereby veiled from guidance, and by His prior decree they act by the deeds of the people of the Fire. Faith is speech and action; they are two things, two systems and two companions that are not separated: there is no faith without action, and no action without faith. Believers differ in faith, and by righteous deeds they increase. They do not leave faith because of sins, nor are they declared disbelievers by committing a major sin or disobedience. The good-doers among them are not granted anything beyond what the Prophet (ﷺ) granted them, and no one among their wrongdoers is witnessed to be in the Fire.

The Qur'an is the speech of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and it is from Allah. It is not created, for what is created perishes. Allah's power, His blessing, and all His attributes are uncreated. They are everlasting and eternal, not newly originated. Our Lord was never deficient so as to increase. His attributes are exalted above resemblance to created beings and fall short of the insight of those who describe Him. He is near in answering when asked, and far in terms of being reached by any who seek Him. His Throne is high, He is distinct from His creation, He exists and is not non-existent or absent. The creatures will die at their appointed times, when their provisions are exhausted and their traces cease. Then, after the squeezing (al-ḍaghṭah) in the graves, they will be questioned. After decay they will be resurrected. On the Day of Resurrection they will be gathered to their Lord, and when they are presented before Him they will be called to account, in the presence of the scales and the unfolding of the scrolls of records. Allah has counted their deeds, and they have forgotten them, on a day whose measure is fifty thousand years. If anyone other than Allah, Mighty and Majestic, were the judge among His creatures, [the matter would be different]. But Allah Himself takes charge of judging between them with His justice, in an amount of time equal to a midday rest in this world, and He is the swiftest of reckoners, just as He originated them, [deciding] who is wretched and who is happy. ﴿On that Day you will return: a party in the Garden and a party in the Blaze.﴾ On that Day the people of the Garden will enjoy blessings, will delight in various kinds of pleasures, and will be honoured with the finest honour. Then they will look toward their Lord. They will have no doubt about the seeing, and they will not dispute it. Their faces will be radiant by His honour, and their eyes will be gazing upon Him by His grace, in everlasting, enduring bliss. ﴿No fatigue will touch them therein, nor will they be removed from it.﴾ ﴿Its fruit is perpetual and its shade; that is the final outcome of those who were mindful [of Allah], and the final outcome of the disbelievers is the Fire.﴾ On that Day the deniers will be veiled from their Lord, and they will be kindled in the Fire. ﴿Evil is what their souls have sent forward for them, that Allah became angry with them, and in the punishment they will abide forever.﴾ They will not be given a decree of death so that they die, nor will their punishment be lightened, except for whomever Allah wills to bring out of it from among the monotheists.

Obedience to those in authority is [required] in what is pleasing to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. One must avoid what provokes His displeasure, must not rebel when they transgress and act unjustly, and must repent to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so that He may incline them to their subjects with compassion. One must refrain from declaring the people of the qibla (ahl al-qiblah, those who face the Ka'bah in prayer) to be disbelievers, and must disassociate from them regarding innovations they have introduced, so long as they have not innovated misguidance. Whoever among them introduces misguidance is outside the people of the qiblah and has exited the religion (māriq, one who has passed through it like an arrow), and one draws near to Allah by disassociating from him. We abandon and avoid his company, for his deception is more dangerous than the deception of war.

It is said: the caliph of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, is preferred first, then ʿUmar. They are the two ministers of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his two companions (buried beside him). Then ʿUthmān, then ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with them all. Then the rest of the ten to whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) guaranteed Paradise. Each one of them receives the amount of love corresponding to the degree of preference that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) assigned to him. Then, after them, all the rest of his Companions, may Allah be pleased with them all. It is said that they are to be praised for their virtues, mentioned for their good deeds, and that one refrains from delving into what occurred between them. They are the best people on earth after their Prophet. Allah chose them and made them helpers of His religion. They are the leaders of the religion and the standard-bearers of the Muslims, may Allah be pleased with them all.

We do not abandon attending Friday prayer and performing it, along with the righteous and the wicked of this nation, so long as one is free from innovation. [We also affirm] jihad alongside every leader, just or unjust, the Hajj, shortening the prayer during travel, and the choice between fasting and breaking the fast [while travelling]. These are doctrines upon which the early leaders of guidance (al-māḍūn al-awwalūn min a'immat al-hudā) agreed. By Allah's grace, the Followers (al-tābiʿūn) held fast to them as a model and in contentment. They avoided excessive speculation in matters they refrained from, so they were guided by Allah's help and were granted success. They did not turn away from following [the Sunnah], lest they fall short, and they did not exceed it, lest they transgress. So we place our trust in Allah, rely upon Him, and in following their traces we desire Him.

This is the explanation of the Sunnah (sharḥ al-sunnah, the way of the Prophet). I have sought to uncover and clarify it. Whoever Allah grants success to uphold what I have set forth, together with His assistance in performing His obligations: taking care to avoid impurities, completing the purifications for acts of worship, performing the prayers as far as one is able, giving zakat to those who possess wealth, performing Hajj for those with means and ability, fasting the month of Ramadan for those who are healthy, [and performing] the five prayers which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) established; the Witr prayer every night; the two rak'ahs of Fajr; the prayers of Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha; the prayer of eclipse; the prayer for rain; avoiding the prohibitions; guarding against gossip, lying, backbiting, and oppression without right, and saying about Allah what you do not know. All of these are grave prohibited sins. [Also] being careful about earnings, food, prohibited things, drinks, and clothing, and avoiding desires, for these lead to committing prohibitions. Whoever grazes around the protected sanctuary is about to fall into it. Whoever is made easy for this, he is upon guidance in the religion, and [has hope] of mercy from the Most Merciful. May Allah grant us and you success to His straightest path, by His abundant ancient favour and His exalted, most generous majesty. Peace be upon you, and the mercy and blessings of Allah. And upon whoever has conveyed greetings to us. The misguided will not attain the peace of Allah the Exalted. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

[The statement of the leader of the Shafiʿis of his time, Abū al-ʿAbbās Ibn Surayj, may Allah have mercy on him]

Abū al-Qāsim Saʿd ibn ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad al-Zanjānī mentioned in the answers to the questions he was asked in Mecca: He said: "All praise is due to Allah, first and last, outwardly and inwardly, and in every state. May Allah's blessings be upon Muḥammad, the chosen one, and upon the good and pure among the Companions and the family. You asked, may Allah support you with His success, for an explanation of what has been established for me and whose reality reaches the one whose path is that of the early generation (al-salaf) and the righteous later generations regarding the attributes mentioned in the revealed Book and the Sunnah transmitted through sound chains by reliable and trustworthy narrators from the Prophet (ﷺ), in a concise statement and a brief answer. So I sought Allah's guidance, may He be glorified and exalted, and I answered with the answer of one of the jurists among the imams, Abū al-ʿAbbās Aḥmad ibn ʿUmar ibn Surayj, may Allah have mercy on him, who was asked a similar question, and he said: 'I say, and with Allah is success: it is forbidden for the intellects to liken Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, and for the imaginations to limit Him, for the conjectures to define Him, for the consciences to probe deeply, for the souls to reflect upon Him, for the thoughts to encompass Him, or for the minds to describe Him, except as He described Himself in His Book or upon the tongue of His Messenger (ﷺ). It is established, confirmed, and clear to all the people of religion, the Sunnah and the community (ahl al-diyānah wa'l-sunnah wa'l-jamāʿah, the People of the Sunnah and the Community), from the early predecessors, the Companions, the Followers, and the rightly guided imams who were well known, up to our time, that all the verses revealed from Allah concerning His essence and attributes, and the authentic reports from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about Allah and His attributes, which were verified by the transmitters and accepted by the trustworthy critics, must be believed by the Muslim believer who has certainty, each one as it has come, and the matter of it must be entrusted to Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, as He commanded. Examples of this are His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Do they wait for anything but that Allah should come to them in shades of clouds, and the angels?﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:210], and His saying: ﴿And your Lord comes, and the angel, rank upon rank﴾ [al-Fajr 89:22], and His saying: ﴿The Most Merciful is established upon the Throne﴾ [Ṭā-Hā 20:5], and His saying: ﴿And the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand﴾ [al-Zumar 39:67], and similar things the Qur'an has stated: such as above-ness (al-fawqiyyah), the Self, the two hands, hearing, sight, speech, the eye, seeing, will, pleasure, anger, love, dislike, care, nearness, distance, displeasure, shame, and nearness as in ﴿two bow-lengths or nearer﴾, the ascent of good words to Him, the ascent of angels and the Spirit to Him, the descent of the Qur'an from Him, His calling of the Prophets, peace be upon them, His speech to the angels, His grasping and His extending, His knowledge, His oneness, His power, His will, His self-sufficiency (ṣamadiyyah), His uniqueness, His being the First and the Last, His being the Outward and the Inward, His life, His endurance, His eternity and His everlastingness, His light, His manifestation, the Face, and the creation of Adam, peace be upon him, with His hand; and like His saying: ﴿Do you feel secure that He who is in the heaven will not cause the earth to swallow you?﴾ [al-Mulk 67:16], and His saying: ﴿And He is the God in the heaven and the God on the earth﴾ [al-Zukhruf 43:84], and His hearing of others and others' hearing of Him, and other attributes connected to Him mentioned in His Book revealed to His Prophet (ﷺ), and all that the Chosen One (ﷺ) uttered of His attributes, such as His planting of the Garden of Paradise with His hand, the Tree of Ṭūbā with His hand, His writing of the Torah with His hand, His laughter and His wonder, His placing of the foot upon the Fire so that it says: 'Enough, enough,' the mention of the fingers, His descent every night to the lowest heaven, the night of Friday, the night of the middle of Shaʿbān, and the Night of Decree; His jealousy, His joy at the repentance of the servant, His veiling with light and with the cloak of majesty, that He is not one-eyed, that He turns away from what He dislikes and does not look at it, that both His hands are right, that Adam chose the right handful, the hadith of the handful, that He has each day such-and-such a glance at the Preserved Tablet, and that on the Day of Resurrection He will scoop three handfuls... and He will admit them into Paradise. When He created Adam, peace be upon him, He wiped his back with His right hand and grasped a handful, and said: 'These are for Paradise, and I do not mind, the companions of the right'; then He grasped another handful and said: 'These are for the Fire, and I do not mind, the companions of the left.' Then He returned them into Adam's loins. [Also] the hadith of the handful by which He brings out from the Fire a people who never did any good, who return as charcoal, and they are cast into a river of Paradise called the River of Life (nahr al-ḥayāh). [Also] the hadith that Adam was created in His image, and His saying: 'Do not disfigure the face, for Allah created the form of the Most Merciful.' [Also] affirming speech with letters and sound, with languages, with words, and with chapters; His speech to Gabriel, the angels, the angel of the wombs, the womb, the angel of death, Riḍwān, Mālik, Adam, Moses, Muḥammad (ﷺ), and to the believer at the reckoning, and in Paradise; the descent of the Qur'an to the lowest heaven; the existence of the Qur'an in the codices; that Allah has not granted permission for anything like His permission for a Prophet who chants the Qur'an beautifully; His saying: 'Allah is more pleased with the reciter of the Qur'an than the owner of a singing slave-girl is with his slave-girl,' and 'Allah loves sneezing and dislikes yawning.' [Also] Allah has finished with the provision and the term. [Also] the hadith of the slaughter of Death and the boasting of Allah, the Exalted, and the ascent of words, deeds and spirits to Him. [Also] the hadith of the Night Journey of the Messenger (ﷺ) in his body and soul, his sight of Paradise and Hell, his reaching the Throne, until there was between him and Allah, the Exalted, nothing but the veil of majesty; the presentation of the Prophets to him, upon him and upon them be the best blessings and peace; and the presentation of the deeds of the community to him; and other things established from him (ﷺ) among the ambiguous reports concerning the attributes of Allah, may He be glorified: whatever has reached us and whatever has not reached us, which is authentically from him, our belief concerning it is [that it is true]. Regarding the ambiguous verses in the Qur'an, we must accept them, not reject them, not interpret them by the interpretation of opponents, not take them to be a likeness of those who liken Allah to creation, not add to them, not subtract from them, not explain them [in detail], not describe their modality (lā nukayyifuhā), not translate His attributes into a language other than Arabic, not point to them by thoughts of the hearts or movements of the limbs. Rather, we affirm what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, affirmed, and we explain what the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions, the Followers and the approved imams of the early generations, known for religion and trustworthiness, explained. We agree on what they agreed upon, we refrain from what they refrained from, and we accept the apparent report and the apparent verse whose revelation is clear. We do not say with the interpretations of the Muʿtazilah (the rationalist school), the Ashʿariyyah, the Jahmiyyah (followers of Jahm ibn Ṣafwān), the heretics (mulḥidah), the Mujassimah (those who anthropomorphize Allah), the Mushabbihah (those who liken Allah to creation), the Karrāmiyyah, or those who ask 'how' (al-kayfiyyah). Rather, we accept them without interpretation, and we believe in them without likening. We say: belief in them is obligatory, speaking of them is a Sunnah, and seeking their interpretation is an innovation."

The last words of Abu al-Abbas ibn Surayj, which Abu al-Qasim Sa'id ibn Ali al-Zanjani (may Allah have mercy on him) related in his answers (ajwibah). Then he mentioned the rest of the questions and their answers.

The Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) are the best of people after the Prophets. The best of them are the ten to whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave the good news of Paradise. The best of these ten are Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, and Ali (may Allah be pleased with them all). We believe in loving the family of Muhammad (ﷺ), his wives, and all of his Companions (may Allah's pleasure be upon them). We mention their virtues, we spread their merits, and we hold our tongues and hearts back from probing into the disputes that arose among them. We ask Allah's forgiveness for them, and we seek nearness to Allah through following them. We hold that jihad, the Friday prayer, and the congregation (jama'ah) will continue until the Day of Resurrection. Listening to and obeying the rulers of the Muslims is obligatory, in obedience to Allah, so long as it is not disobedience to Him. It is not permissible to rebel against them or to separate from them. We do not declare any Muslim to be a disbeliever (takfir) because of a sin he has committed, even a grave one. We do not abstain from praying over them (the funeral prayer). Rather, we judge them according to the ruling of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). We ask Allah's mercy for Mu'awiyah, and we leave the inner state (sarirah) of Yazid to Allah the Exalted. It has been related from him that when he saw the head of al-Husayn (may Allah's pleasure be upon him), he said: "The one who severed the ties of kinship between you and him has killed you." We disavow those who killed al-Husayn (may Allah's pleasure be upon him), who helped in it, or who instigated it, whether openly or secretly. This is our belief, and we leave their inner state to Allah the Exalted.

The comprehensive formula in the field of tawhid (affirmation of Allah's oneness) is to say: affirmation without anthropomorphism (tashbih), and negation without denial (ta'til). Allah the Exalted says: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾ [al-Shura: 11]. The comprehensive formula concerning the ambiguous (mutashabih) verses about the divine attributes is to say: "I believe in what Allah the Exalted has said, according to what He intended, and I believe in what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has said, according to what he intended." This is our belief, to which we hold fast and upon which we rest. We ask Allah the Exalted to give us life upon it, to cause us to die upon it, and to make it our means of intercession on the Day of standing before Him. Indeed He is Generous and Bountiful. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

[The statement of the Imam Isma'il ibn Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Taymi]

He is the author of the book al-Targhib wal-Tarhib and the book al-Hujjah fi Bayan al-Mahajjah, and of the doctrine of the People of the Sunnah (Ahl al-Sunnah). He was an imam of the Shafi'is in his time, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him. Abu Musa al-Madini compiled excellent virtues for him because of his greatness. He said in the book al-Hujjah, in a chapter on the explanation of Allah the Glorified and Exalted's istiwa' (being established) upon the Throne: Allah the Exalted says: ﴿The Most Merciful is established upon the Throne﴾ [Ta-Ha: 5]. He also said, in another verse: ﴿His Footstool encompasses the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255], and He said: ﴿Indeed He is Most High, All-Wise﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 4].

And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ [al-A'la: 1]. The People of the Sunnah said: Allah is above the heavens. None of His creation is above Him. Among the evidence for this is that people point to the sky with their fingers, call upon Him, and raise their heads and eyes toward Him. Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿He is the Subjugator over His servants﴾ [al-An'am: 18]. And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Do you feel secure that He who is in the heaven will not cause the earth to swallow you while it shakes? Or do you feel secure that He who is in the heaven will not send against you a storm of stones? Then you will know how My warning was﴾ [al-Mulk: 16-17]. The evidence for this is also the verses that mention the descent of revelation.

A section on the explanation that the Throne is above the heavens, and that Allah the Glorified and Exalted is above the Throne. He then mentioned the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him), which is in al-Bukhari: "When Allah had decreed creation, He wrote in a Book, which is with Him above the Throne: 'Indeed My mercy has overcome My wrath.'" He extensively argued for this from the Sunnah. Then he said: The scholars of the Sunnah said: Indeed Allah the Mighty and Majestic is established upon His Throne, separate from His creation. The Mu'tazilah said: He is in His essence (bi-dhatihi) in every place.

He said: The Ash'ariyyah said: the istiwa' refers to the Throne. He said: If it were as they say, the recitation would have been with the Throne in the nominative case (raf'), but since it is in the genitive (khafd), this indicates that it refers back to Allah the Glorified and Exalted. He said: Some of them said: istawa means istawla (to take control). The poet said:

"Bishr has taken control over Iraq,
without sword or spilled blood."

Taking control is only ascribed to one who gains power over something after being unable to, whereas Allah the Exalted has always been capable of all things and in control of them. Do you not see that one is not described as taking control of Iraq unless he was previously unable to do so? Then Abu al-Qasim related from Dhu al-Nun al-Misri that he was asked: "What did Allah the Glorified intend by creating the Throne?" He said: "He intended that the hearts of the knowers would not be bewildered (tatuh)." He said: It was related from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) in explaining the verse: ﴿There is no secret conversation between three but that He is the fourth of them﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 7], that he said: "He is upon the Throne, and His knowledge is in every place." Then he presented arguments from reports, until he said: These people claim that the meaning of ﴿The Most Merciful is established upon the Throne﴾ [Ta-Ha: 5] is that He owns it, and that He has no more special relation to the Throne than to any other place. This nullifies the singling out and honoring of the Throne.

The People of the Sunnah said: Allah the Exalted created the heavens, and His Throne was created before the creation of the heavens and the earth. Then He established Himself upon the Throne after creating the heavens and the earth, as the text has reported. Its meaning is not contact (mumassah). Rather, He is established upon His Throne without modality (bila kayf), as He informed about Himself.

He said: These people claim that it is not permissible to point toward Allah the Glorified upward with heads and fingers, because that implies delimitation (tahdid). Yet the Muslims have unanimously agreed that Allah the Glorified is the Most High, the Exalted, and the Quran has affirmed this. These people claim that this means the highness of domination (uluww al-ghalabah), not the highness of essence. According to the Muslims, Allah the Mighty and Majestic has the highness of domination, and highness in all its aspects, because highness is an attribute of praise. Thus it is established that Allah the Exalted has highness of essence, highness of attributes, and highness of domination and subjugation. In their denial of pointing toward Allah the Glorified and Exalted from the direction of above, they oppose all other religious communities (milal). The majority of Muslims and all other religious communities have reached consensus on pointing toward Allah the Glorified and Exalted from the direction above, in supplication and asking. Their unanimous agreement on this is a proof. No one has considered pointing toward Him from below or from any other direction other than above to be permissible. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿They fear their Lord above them﴾ [al-Nahl: 50]. And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿To Him ascends the good word﴾ [Fatir: 10]. And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 4]. Allah the Exalted also related that Pharaoh said: ﴿O Haman, build for me a tower that I may reach the means, the means to the heavens, and look at the God of Moses﴾ [Ghafir: 36-37]. Pharaoh had understood from Moses (peace be upon him) that he affirmed a God above the heaven, to the extent that he wished with his tower to ascend to Him, and he accused Moses (peace be upon him) of lying about this. The Jahmiyyah do not know that Allah is above them by the existence of His essence, so their understanding is more deficient than that of Pharaoh (indeed, even more misguided). It is authentically related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he asked the slave girl whose master wished to free her: "Where is Allah?" She said: "In the heaven," and she pointed with her head to the sky. He said: "Who am I?" She said: "You are the Messenger of Allah." He said: "Free her, for she is a believer." So the Prophet (ﷺ) ruled that she was a believer when she said that Allah is in the heaven, and the Jahmi ruled that whoever says this is a disbeliever. All of this is the words of Abu al-Qasim al-Taymi (may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him).

[A section on the statement of the Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal and his companions (may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him)]

Al-Khallal said in *Kitab al-Sunnah*: Yusuf ibn Musa narrated to us (he said): Abdullah ibn Ahmad informed us, saying: It was said to my father: "Our Lord, blessed and exalted, is above the seventh heaven, upon His Throne, separate from His creation, and His power and His knowledge are in every place?" He said: "Yes. Nothing is outside of His knowledge."

Al-Khallal said: Abd al-Malik ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Maymuni informed me, saying: I asked Abu Abdullah Ahmad about someone who says that Allah, exalted is He, is not upon the Throne. He said: "All of his speech revolves around disbelief."

Abu al-Qasim al-Tabari al-Shafi'i narrated in his *Kitab al-Sunnah*, with his chain, from Hanbal, who said: It was asked of Abu Abdullah: "What is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿There is no secret conversation among three but that He is the fourth of them﴾ [al-Mujadila: 7], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He is with you﴾ [al-Hadid: 4]?" He said: "His knowledge encompasses everything, and our Lord is upon the Throne without limit and without attribute. His Footstool encompasses the heavens and the earth."

Abu Talib said: I asked Ahmad ibn Hanbal about a man who said: "Allah is with us," and he recited His saying: ﴿There is no secret conversation among three but that He is the fourth of them﴾ [al-Mujadila: 7]. He said: "They take the last part of the verse and leave its beginning. Why did you not recite to him: ﴿Do you not see that Allah knows what is in the heavens﴾ [al-Mujadila: 7]? So His knowledge is with them." He also said, regarding Qaf: ﴿And We know what his soul whispers to him, and We are closer to him than his jugular vein﴾ [Qaf: 16].

Al-Marwazi said: I said to Abu Abdullah: "A man said: 'I say as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿There is no secret conversation among three but that He is the fourth of them, nor among five but that He is the sixth of them﴾ [al-Mujadila: 7]. I say this and do not go beyond it to anything else.'" Abu Abdullah said: "This is the speech of the Jahmiyyah." I said to him: "Then how should we say ﴿There is no secret conversation among three but that He is the fourth of them, nor among five but that He is the sixth of them﴾ [al-Mujadila: 7]?" He said: "His knowledge is in every place, and His knowledge is with them." He said: "The beginning of the verse indicates that it is His knowledge."

He also said in another place: "Allah, exalted and majestic, is upon His Throne above the seventh heaven. He knows what is beneath the lowest earth. He is not touching anything of His creation. He, blessed and exalted, is separate from His creation, and His creation is separate from Him."

In the book *al-Radd ʿala al-Jahmiyya* (The Refutation of the Jahmiyyah), which Khallal narrated from him through his son Abdullah, he said: "Chapter: Explaining what the Jahmiyyah deny, that Allah, exalted is He, is upon the Throne. We say to them: 'What do you deny about Allah, exalted is He, being upon the Throne, when He, exalted is He, has said: ﴿The Most Merciful is established upon the Throne﴾ [Taha: 5]?' They said: 'He is beneath the seventh earth just as He is upon the Throne, and in the heavens and the earth, and in every place,' and he recited: ﴿And He is Allah in the heavens and on the earth﴾ [al-An'am: 3]."

Ahmad said: "We said: 'The Muslims know many places in which there is none of the greatness of the Lord: your bodies, your bellies, the latrines and the filthy places. In them there is none of the greatness of the Lord, exalted is He. Yet Allah, mighty and majestic, has informed us that He is in the heaven, when He said: ﴿Are you secure from the One who is in the heaven that He will cause the earth to swallow you, and behold, it shakes? Or are you secure from the One who is in the heaven?﴾ [al-Mulk: 16]," and the verse continues. And He said: ﴿To Him ascends the good word﴾ [Fatir: 10]. And He said: ﴿Indeed, I will take you and raise you to Me﴾ [Al 'Imran: 55], ﴿But Allah raised him to Himself﴾ [al-Nisa': 158], and ﴿They fear their Lord above them﴾ [al-Nahl: 50].

Abu Bakr al-Khallal mentioned this entire book in his *Kitab al-Sunnah*, in which he gathered the texts and statements of Ahmad. In the same manner, al-Bayhaqi gathered, in his book which he named *Jami' al-Nusus min Kalam al-Shafi'i* (The Compendium of Texts from the Speech of al-Shafi'i), and these are two magnificent books that no scholar can do without. The preface of the book of Ahmad ibn Hanbal reads: "Praise be to Allah, who has placed in every era, during the intervals between the messengers, peace be upon them, remnants of the people of knowledge who call the one who has gone astray to guidance and who bear the harm inflicted on them with patience. They revive the dead (hearts) with the Book of Allah and give sight with the light of Allah to the people of blindness. How many a slain one of Iblis have they revived, and how many a lost wanderer have they guided! How beautiful are their traces upon the people, and how ugly are the traces of the people upon them. They negate from the Book of Allah, exalted is He, the distortion of the misguided, the appropriation of the falsifiers, and the interpretation of the ignorant, who have raised the banners of innovation and let loose the reins of strife. They disagree concerning the Book, oppose the Book, and are unanimous in opposing the Book. They speak about Allah, and about Allah, and about the Book of Allah, exalted is He, without knowledge. They speak the ambiguous (mutashabih) speech, and they deceive the ignorant with what they make confusing for them. We seek refuge in Allah from the trials of the misleaders." Then he said: "Chapter: Explaining what the Jahmiyyah, the heretics (zanadiqa), went astray in regarding the ambiguous (mutashabih) verses of the Qur'an." Then he spoke about His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins﴾ [al-Nisa': 56].

He said: "The heretics said: 'What is the matter with their skins that have disobeyed and have been burned? Allah has replaced them with other skins. We see nothing but that Allah, mighty and majestic, is punishing skins without any sin, when He says: "other skins" [al-Nisa': 56].' So they doubted the Qur'an and claimed that it is contradictory. We said: 'The saying of Allah, mighty and majestic, ﴿We will replace them with other skins﴾ [al-Nisa': 56] does not mean other skins besides their skins. Rather, by replacing them He means renewing them, because when their skins are roasted through, Allah renews them.'" Then he spoke about verses from the difficult (mushkil) parts of the Qur'an. Then he said: "Among what the misguided Jahmiyyah denied is that Allah, mighty and majestic, is established upon the Throne, while He has said: ﴿The Most Merciful is established upon the Throne﴾ [Taha: 5], and He has said: ﴿Then the Most Merciful established Himself upon the Throne; so ask about Him one who is informed﴾ [al-Furqan: 59]." Then he cited the proofs of the Qur'an. Then he said: "We found that everything below is blameworthy. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire﴾ [al-Nisa': 145], and He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And those who disbelieved will say: 'Our Lord, show us those who misled us from among the jinn and mankind; we will put them under our feet so that they will be among the lowest﴾ [Fussilat: 29]."

Then he said: "The meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He is Allah in the heavens and on the earth. He knows your secrets and what you openly declare, and He knows what you earn﴾ [al-An'am: 3], is: He is the God of those in the heavens, and the God of those on the earth. He is upon the Throne, and His knowledge encompasses what is below the Throne. No place is outside of His knowledge, and the knowledge of Allah, exalted is He, is not in one place rather than another. This is from His saying: ﴿That you may know that Allah is capable of all things and that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge﴾ [al-Talaq: 12]."

Imam Ahmad said: "Among the considerations on this matter: if a man had in his hand a glass vessel containing something, the gaze of the son of Adam would encompass the glass without the son of Adam being inside the glass. So Allah, glorified is He, and to Him belongs the highest likeness, encompasses all that He has created, and knows how it is and what it is, without being in anything of what He has created." He said: "Another quality: if a man built a house with all its facilities and then closed its door, nothing in the house would be hidden from him, how many rooms are in his house and how large each room is, without the owner of the house being inside the house. So Allah, glorified is He, encompasses all that He has created, knows how it is and what it is, and to Him belongs the highest likeness, and He is not in anything of what He has created."

Imam Ahmad said: "Among what the Jahmiyyah interpreted from the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿There is no secret conversation among three but that He is the fourth of them﴾ [al-Mujadila: 7], they said: 'Allah is with us and in us.' We said to them: 'Why have you cut off the report from its beginning? Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Do you not see that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth? There is no secret conversation among three but that He is the fourth of them, nor among five but that He is the sixth of them, nor is there less than that or more but that He is with them wherever they are﴾ [al-Mujadila: 7],' and the verse continues, meaning His knowledge is with them wherever they are: ﴿Then He will inform them of what they did on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things﴾ [al-Mujadila: 7]. So He opened the report with His knowledge and closed it with His knowledge."

Imam Ahmad said: "If you want to know that the Jahmi is lying against Allah, glorified and exalted is He, when he claims that He is in every place and is not in one place rather than another, then say to him: 'Was Allah there when there was nothing?' He will say: 'Yes.' Then say to him: 'When He created the creation, did He create it within Himself or outside of Himself?' He will then arrive at one of three positions. If he claims that Allah, exalted is He, created the creation within Himself, he has disbelieved when he claims that the jinn, mankind, the devils and Iblis are within the essence of Allah. (If he says: 'He created them outside of Himself, then entered among them,' he has also disbelieved, when he claims that He entered every desolate and filthy place.) If he says: 'He created them outside of Himself and did not enter among them,' he has retracted his whole statement entirely, and this is the position of the People of the Sunnah."

Ahmad said: "Chapter: Explaining what is mentioned in the Qur'an: 'And He is with you.' This is in several aspects. Allah, exalted is He, said to Musa and Harun, peace be upon them both: ﴿Indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see﴾ [Taha: 46], meaning: in defending you both. And He said: ﴿The second of two, when they were in the cave, when he said to his companion, 'Do not grieve; indeed, Allah is with us'﴾ [al-Tawbah: 40], meaning: in defending us. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And Allah is with the patient﴾ [al-Baqarah: 249], meaning: in giving them victory over their enemy. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you will be superior, and Allah is with you﴾ [Muhammad: 35], meaning: in giving you victory over your enemy. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And He is with them when they plot by night what He does not approve of in speech﴾ [al-Nisa': 108], meaning: He says with His knowledge concerning them. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 62], meaning: with help against Pharaoh.

When the proof was established against the Jahmi regarding what he claimed about Allah, glorified is He, that He is with His creation, he said: 'He is in everything, not touching anything and not separate from anything.' We said to him: 'If He is not separate from mankind, is He touching them?' He said: 'No.' We said: 'How can He be in everything, neither touching anything nor separate from anything?' He did not answer well. Then he said: 'Without how,' so that he might deceive the ignorant with this phrase and obscure matters for them. Then we said to him: 'When the Day of Resurrection comes, will not the Garden, the Fire, the Throne and the desires be? He said: "Yes." We said: "Where will our Lord be?" He said: "He will be in everything, just as He was when the world existed."'"
