But it is also part of Allah's wisdom that He stripped the intellects of many of these people of their proper quality, veiled them from knowing Him, and confined them to the apparent side of knowledge of the present life, while they are heedless of the Hereafter because of its lowliness, baseness and insignificance, and their lack of capacity for knowing Him, knowing His names and attributes, and the secrets of His religion and law. Bounty is in the hand of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is the Lord of tremendous bounty.

This is a domain of which creation can never grasp anything whose relation to what is hidden from them is significant. Rather, the knowledge of the first and the last of them about it is like the drop of a sparrow from the sea. Yet this does not necessitate turning away from it or despairing of it. Rather, the intelligent person derives from what has become apparent to him of it an indication of what lies beyond it.

((Part Thirteen))

(Fasl)

When the appointed term that God has decreed for him is reached and fulfilled, the messengers of his Lord, mighty and majestic, come to him to transfer him from the abode of perishing to the abode of permanence. They sit before him as far as the eye can see. Then the angel entrusted with seizing souls draws near to him and summons the soul. If it is a good soul, he says: "Come out, O good soul, that was in a good body. Come out praiseworthy, and rejoice in rest (rawh), sweet fragrance (rayhan), and a Lord who is not angry." It leaves his body as a drop leaves the mouth of a waterskin. When he takes it, the messengers do not leave it in his hands for the blink of an eye. They wrap it in spices (hanut) and a shroud (kafan) from Paradise. Then they pray over it, and there is found from it the finest scent of musk that has ever been found on the face of the earth. They then ascend with it to the first assembly, with the swiftest of the reckoners. It reaches the lowest heaven, asks permission on its behalf, and the gates of heaven are opened for it. The angels of that heaven pray over it, and those closest to God accompany it to the second heaven, where the same is done. Then the third, then the fourth, until it reaches the heaven in which God, the Mighty and Majestic, is. It greets its Lord, blessed and exalted, with the greeting of lordship: "O Allah, You are Peace, and from You is peace. Blessed are You, O Possessor of majesty and honour." If God wills, He permits it to prostrate. Then the decree of Paradise is issued for it, and the Lord, majestic in His majesty, says: "Write the book of My servant in 'Illiyyin. Then return him to the earth, for from it I created them, into it I return them, and from it I bring them forth once more." Then his soul returns to the earth, and it witnesses his washing, his shrouding, his carrying and his preparation for burial.

He says: "Hasten me, hasten me." When he is placed in his grave niche (lahd) and his companions turn away from him, the soul returns with him, so that he hears the sound of their sandals on the ground. Then the two angels of the grave (fattanan al-qabr) come to him, seat him, and ask him: "Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your prophet?" He says: "My Lord is Allah, my religion is Islam, and my prophet is Muhammad." They confirm him and give him the good news that this is what he lived upon, died upon, and will be raised upon.

Then his grave is widened for him as far as his eye can see, a green carpet is spread for him, and there is assigned to him a handsome young man of good face and fine scent. He says: "Rejoice in what pleases you." He asks: "Who are you? Your face is a face that brings good." He replies: "I am your righteous deed." Then a window to the Fire is opened for him, and it is said: "Look at what Allah has turned away from you." Then a window to Paradise is opened for him, and it is said: "Look at what Allah has prepared for you." So he sees both.

As for the wicked soul, it is the opposite of all that. When it is permitted to depart, there descend upon it angels with black faces, with spices of fire and a shroud of fire. They sit before it as far as the eye can see. Then the angel entrusted with seizing souls draws near, summons it, and says: "Come out, O wicked soul, that was in a wicked body. Rejoice in boiling water (hamim), in the dark liquid (ghassaq), and in other punishments of their kind, in pairs." It scatters through the body, and he draws it out from the depths of the body, so that the veins and sinews are severed with it, as a thorn is pulled out of wet wool. When he takes it, he does not leave it in his hand for the blink of an eye. It is found to smell like the foulest stench of a carcass on the face of the earth. It is wrapped in that spice and bound in that shroud. Every angle between heaven and earth curses it. Then it is taken up to heaven, and it asks for the gates to be opened, but they are not opened for it. Then a call comes from the Lord of the worlds: "Write its book in Sijjin, and return it to the earth." So its soul is cast down violently. It witnesses its own preparation, shrouding and carrying, and while it is on the bier it says: "Woe to it! Where are you taking it?" When it is placed in the niche, the soul is returned to him, and the two angels come to him, ask him about his Lord, his religion and his prophet. He stammers and says: "I do not know." They say: "You did not know, nor did you recite." Then they strike him a blow, and he gives a cry that every thing hears except the two weighty ones (humans and jinn). Then his grave constricts upon him until his ribs interlock. Then a fire is spread for him, and a window to Paradise is opened, and it is said: "Look at what Allah has turned away from you." Then a window to the Fire is opened, and it is said: "Look at your place in the Fire." So he sees both. Then there is assigned to him a blind, deaf, mute one. He asks: "Who are you? Your face is a face that brings evil." He replies: "I am your evil deed."

Then the believer is blessed in the barzakh (intermediate realm) according to his deeds, and the wicked one is punished in it according to his deeds. Each limb is singled out for a punishment fitting its transgression. The lips of backbiters, who tear apart the flesh of people and assail their honour, are cut with scissors of fire. The bellies of those who consume the wealth of orphans are set ablaze with fire. Those who consume usury are made to swallow stones, and they swim in rivers of blood as they swam in illicit gain. The heads of those who sleep through the obligatory prayer are crushed with a great stone. The jaw of the liar who tells a great lie is split with iron hooks, its back, nostril and eye split to the back of the head, just as his lie spread in every direction. Adulterous women are suspended by their breasts, and fornicating men and women are confined in a heated oven, where the organ of sin is punished, which is the lowest part of them.

And worries, griefs, sorrows and inner pains are imposed upon the idle souls that were busied with frivolity, play and idleness. Pain works in their souls as vermin and worms work in their flesh, until Allah, glorified is He, permits the end of the age of the world and the folding up of this life. Then the earth rains a heavy, white rain like the seed of men for forty mornings, and they sprout from their graves as a plant and herbage sprout. When the embryos are completed and the mother is about to give birth, and the time of delivery comes, Allah, glorified is He, commands Israfil, who blows into the Trumpet (Sur) with the blast of resurrection. This is the third blast; before it was the blast of death, and before that the blast of terror. The earth splits open over them, and they are standing, looking. The believer says: "Praise be to Allah, who has given us life after He caused us to die, and to Him is the resurrection."

The disbeliever says: ﴿Woe to us! Who has raised us from our resting place? This is what the Most Merciful promised, and the messengers spoke truly.﴾

They are driven to the place of gathering, barefoot, naked and uncircumcised, with every soul accompanied by a driver who drives it and a witness who testifies against it. Some are joyful and some are wretched, some laughing and some weeping. ﴿Faces that Day will be bright, laughing, rejoicing; and faces that Day will have dust upon them, darkness covering them.﴾ When their number is complete and they are all upon the face of the earth, the heaven splits open, the stars scatter, and the angels of the heaven descend and surround them. Then the angels of the second heaven descend and surround the angels of the lowest heaven. Then each heaven is likewise. While they are in this state, the Lord of the worlds, glorified is He, comes to judge decisively. The earth shines with His light, the criminals are separated from the believers, the scale is set up, the register is brought, and witnesses are summoned. On that Day the hands, tongues, feet and skins bear witness. The dispute before Allah, glorified is He, does not cease until the soul and the body dispute with one another. The body says: "I was only a corpse; I did not understand, hear or see. You were the one who heard, saw and understood, and you directed me wherever you wished." The soul replies: "It was you who acted, committed the sin, and struck."

Then Allah, glorified is He, sends to them an angel to judge between them. He says: "Your example is like a seeing man who is lame and a blind man who is healthy, who entered a garden. The lame one said: 'I see the fruits but I cannot rise to them.' The blind one said: 'I can rise, but I see nothing.' The lame one said to him: 'Carry me until I reach them,' and they did so. On whom then will the punishment fall?" They say: "On both of them." He says: "So it is with you two."

Then Allah, glorified is He, judges among His servants with the judgment for which all the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth praise Him, and every pious and wicked, believer and disbeliever. ﴿And every soul will be paid in full for what it did.﴾ ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.﴾

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 32, verses 16–17 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted said concerning the lovers (al-muhibbin): ﴿Their sides forsake their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and in hope﴾.

When their sides forsook their beds, the sides (of the body) forsook them, and they made them serve, and commanded them, and they obeyed.

The poet said:
"My day is the day of people, until, when night appears to me, the beds draw me to you."

It is related that one of the righteous passed by a mosque and saw Satan standing at its door, unable to enter. He looked, and there was a man sleeping and another standing in prayer. He said to him: "Does this one who prays prevent you from entering?" He said: "No, it is that crouching lion that prevents me. Were it not for his place, I would have entered."

In sum, the heart of the lover is always on a journey without end toward his Beloved. Whenever he crosses one stage and station, another appears to him, as it has been said:
"When you cross one sign, another sign appears."

He is a traveler among his family, a wayfarer while in his home, and a stranger while among his brothers and kin. He sees everyone as belonging to him, yet he does not see himself as belonging to anyone. The strength of the lover's attachment to his Beloved requires that his heart not settle short of reaching Him. Whenever his movements calm and his preoccupations lessen, the affairs of his heart gather upon him, and indeed his journey toward his Beloved grows stronger.

(Admonition)
A journey is only completed, and the traveler only arrives, by keeping to the highway and traveling by night. If the traveler strays from the road and sleeps the whole night, when will he reach his destination?

(Section: That Paradise is beyond what occurs to the mind or what passes through the imagination)
And that the place of a whip's length in it is better than the world and what is in it.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and in hope, and from what We have provided them they spend. No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do﴾.

Consider how He matched what they hid of night prayer with the reward He hid for them, which no soul knows. And how He matched their anxiety, fear, and restlessness upon their beds, when they rise for the night prayer, with the coolness of eyes in Paradise.

In the Two Sahihs (al-Sahihayn, Bukhari and Muslim), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, Allah the Mighty and Majestic said:
"I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived."
The confirmation of this in the Book of Allah is: ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do﴾.

In another wording in both: Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: "I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived, as a treasure, apart from what I have revealed to you." Then he recited: ﴿No soul knows﴾.

In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi, who said: "I witnessed with the Prophet (ﷺ) a gathering in which Paradise was described, until he finished. Then he said at the end of his speech about it: 'what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.' Then he recited this verse: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and in hope, and from what We have provided them they spend. No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do﴾."

In the Two Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:
"A bow's length of one of you in Paradise is better than what the sun rises upon or sets upon."

The hadith of Abu Umamah from the Prophet (ﷺ) has already preceded: "Whoever exerts himself for Paradise, for by the Lord of the Ka'bah, Paradise has no equal. It is a light that shines, a fragrant herb that sways, a lofty palace, a flowing river, ripe fruit, a beautiful and lovely spouse, many garments, a dwelling forever in an abode of peace, fruits, greenery, joy, blessing, and an elevated, radiant dwelling." And if there were nothing of Paradise's worth and nobility except that it is not asked for by the Face of Allah other than itself, that would be a sufficient honor and virtue.

And as in Sunan Abi Dawud, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn Mu'adh ibn al-Mundhir, from Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:
"Nothing is asked by the Face of Allah except Paradise."

In Mu'jam al-Tabarani, from the hadith of Baqiyyah, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:
"When Allah created the Garden of Eden, He created in it what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. Then He said to it: 'Speak.' It said: 'The believers have indeed prospered.'"

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "A place of a whip in Paradise is better than the world and what is in it."

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, Hammam narrated to us from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:
"The lash of one of your whips in Paradise is better than what is between the heaven and the earth."
And this chain is according to the conditions of the Two Sahihs.

Al-Tirmidhi said: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Ibn Lahi'ah informed us from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Dawud ibn 'Amir ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said:
"If the smallest fingernail of what is in Paradise appeared, it would adorn everything between the horizons of the heavens and the earth. And if a man of the people of Paradise looked out and his bracelets appeared, he would obscure the light of the sun as the sun obscures the light of the stars."
Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan gharib hadith. We do not know it with this chain except from the hadith of Ibn Lahi'ah.
Yahya ibn Ayyub has narrated this hadith from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, and said from Amr ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from the Prophet (ﷺ).
I say: Ibn Wahb has also narrated it: Amr, that is Ibn al-Harith, informed us that Sulayman ibn Humayd narrated to him that 'Amir ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas said, Sulayman said: "I do not know except that he narrated to me from his father, from the Messenger of Allah, from the Messenger of Allah, that he said:
'If a fingernail of Paradise appeared to the world, it would adorn what is between the heaven and the earth.'"
And on this topic there are reports from Anas ibn Malik, Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, and 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As.

How can the worth of an abode be measured, which Allah planted with His Hand, made a dwelling for His beloved ones, and filled with His mercy, honors, and good pleasure? He described its bliss as the great triumph, its kingdom as the great dominion, deposited in it all good in its entirety, and purified it from every defect, blemish, and deficiency.

If you ask about its earth and soil, it is musk and saffron. If you ask about its ceiling, it is the Throne of the Merciful. If you ask about its paving, it is pure musk. If you ask about its pebbles, they are pearls and gems. If you ask about its building, it is a brick of silver and a brick of gold. If you ask about its trees, there is no tree whose trunk is not of gold and silver, not of firewood or timber. If you ask about its fruit, it is like large jars, softer than butter and sweeter than honey. If you ask about its leaves, they are finer than the most delicate garments. If you ask about its rivers, they are rivers of milk whose taste never changes, rivers of wine, a delight for drinkers, and rivers of purified honey. If you ask about their food, it is fruit of their choosing and the flesh of birds they desire. If you ask about their drink, it is Tasnim, ginger, and camphor. If you ask about their vessels, they are vessels of gold and silver in the clarity of crystal. If you ask about the width of its doors, between the two panels is a forty years' journey, and a day will come upon it when it is crowded with throngs. If you ask about the rustling of the winds in its trees, they stir delight in whoever hears them. If you ask about its shade, there is one tree under whose shade a swift, vigorous rider travels for a hundred years without crossing it. If you ask about its vastness, its least inhabitant moves through his kingdom, couches, palaces, and gardens for a distance of two thousand years. If you ask about its tents and domes, one tent is a hollow pearl, sixty miles long, among those tents. If you ask about its high chambers and pavilions, they are upper rooms above upper rooms, built, with rivers flowing beneath them. If you ask about its height, look at the star rising or setting on the horizon that eyes can hardly reach. If you ask about the clothing of its people, it is silk and gold. If you ask about their bedding, its linings are of thick brocade, spread out in the highest ranks. If you ask about their couches, they are beds with canopies, which are curtained chambers fastened with golden buttons, having no gaps or crevices. If you ask about the faces of its people and their beauty, they are in the form of the moon. If you ask about their teeth, they are the sons of thirty-three, in the form of Adam, peace be upon him, the father of mankind. If you ask about their listening, it is the singing of their wives, the Wide-eyed Houris, and above that the hearing of the voices of the angels and the prophets, and above both, the speech of the Lord of the worlds. If you ask about their mounts on which they visit one another, they are swift camels, by Allah's will, that carry them wherever they wish in the gardens. If you ask about their ornaments and emblems, they are bracelets of gold and pearls, and on their heads are crowns. If you ask about their young servants, they are everlasting youths, as if they were hidden pearls. If you ask about their brides and spouses, they are the full-breasted maidens of equal age, through whose limbs the water of youth flows. For the rose and the apple is what their cheeks wear, for the pomegranate is what their breasts hold, for the strung pearls is what their mouths contain, and for delicacy and slenderness is what their waists encircle. The sun runs through the beauties of their faces when they appear, and lightning flashes between their front teeth when they smile. When she faces her lover, say whatever you wish about the meeting of two luminaries; and when she speaks to him, what do you imagine of the conversation of two beloveds? If she embraces him, what do you imagine of the entwining of two branches? He sees his face in the cheek of her, as one sees in a mirror that its polisher has burnished. He sees the marrow of her shin through the flesh; neither her skin nor her bone nor her garments conceal it. If she looked out upon the world, she would fill what is between the earth and the heaven with fragrance, make the mouths of creation utter tahlil, takbir, and tasbih, adorn what is between the two horizons, and cause every eye to look away from all else, and she would obscure the light of the sun as the sun obscures the light of the stars. She would have greeted with the living, self-subsisting Allah all who stand upon her back. Her veil upon her head is better than the world and what is in it, and her union is more desirable to him than all his wishes. She does not increase over the long ages except in beauty and loveliness, and the length of time only increases her in love and union. She is free from menstruation, childbirth, the monthly course, and postnatal bleeding, purified from mucus, spittle, urine, feces, and all other impurities. Her youth does not fade, her garments do not wear out, the garment of her beauty does not decay, and the sweetness of her union does not bore. She has restricted her gaze to her husband, so she does not look at anyone else, and he has restricted his gaze to her; she is the ultimate object of his wish and desire. If he looks at her, she delights him; if he commands her to obey him, she obeys him; if he is absent from her, she guards him. So she is with him in the ultimate of hopes and security. Moreover, no human or jinn has touched her before him. Whenever he looks at her, she fills his heart with joy, and whenever she speaks to him, she fills his ear with scattered and arranged pearls. When she appears, she fills the palace and the upper chamber with light. If you ask about her age, she is of equal age in the finest prime of youth. If you ask about beauty, have you seen the sun and the moon? If you ask about her eyes, they are the most beautiful black in the clearest white, with the most lovely gaze. If you ask about her stature, have you seen the finest branches? If you ask about her breasts, they are full-breasted maidens whose breasts are like the tenderest pomegranates. If you ask about her complexion, it is like the ruby and coral. If you ask about the beauty of her character, they are the good, beautiful women who combine beauty with kindness, given the beauty of inner and outer self, so they are the joy of souls and the coolness of eyes. If you ask about the goodness of companionship and the pleasure found there, they are the women who make themselves beloved to their husbands with a gentle affection that blends with the spirit in a manner beyond description. So what do you imagine of a woman who, when she laughs in the face of her husband, lights up Paradise with her laughter, and when she moves from one palace to another, you would say: this is the sun moving through the constellations of its sphere? When she is in the presence of her husband, how sweet is that presence, and if she embraces him, how delightful is that embrace and close contact!
Their poet said:
"Her talk is lawful magic; if it had not produced the killing of the cautious Muslim,
If it lasts long, it does not weary; and if she speaks, the speaker wishes she did not finish."
If she sings, how delightful to sight and hearing! If she is companionable and delights, how sweet that companionship and delight! If she kisses, nothing is more desirable to him than that kiss; if she gives, nothing is sweeter or better than that giving. Moreover, if you ask about the Day of Increase (yawm al-mazid), the increase of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy, and the vision of His Face, which is exalted above likeness and resemblance, as you see the sun at midday and the moon on the night of the full moon, as the truthful and believed one (al-sadiq al-masduq) has transmitted reports about it, this is found in the sound collections, the Sunan, and the Musnads, from the narrations of Jarir, Suhayb, Anas, Abu Hurayrah, and Abu Musa and Abu Sa'id. So listen: on the day when the caller calls, "O people of Paradise! Your Lord, blessed and exalted, wishes to visit you, so come to His visitation." They will say: "We hear and obey." They will rise hastening to the visitation, and behold, swift camels have been prepared for them. They mount them swiftly, until they reach the spacious valley that was made their appointment. They gather there, and the caller leaves none of them behind. The Lord, blessed and exalted, commands His Throne, and it is set up there. Then pulpits of light are set up for them, pulpits of pearl, pulpits of chrysolite, pulpits of gold, and pulpits of silver. The least of them sits on mounds of musk, and far be it that anyone among them be lowly. They do not see that the owners of the thrones are above them in gifts. When their seats are settled and their places are at rest, the caller calls: "O people of Paradise! For you there is a promise with Allah which He wishes to fulfill for you." They will say: "What is it? Has He not whitened our faces, made our scales heavy, admitted us into Paradise, and removed us from the Fire?" While they are like that, a light shines upon them, and Paradise is illuminated by it. They raise their heads, and behold, the Almighty, exalted in majesty and sanctified in His names, has looked down upon them from above and said: "O people of Paradise, peace be upon you." This greeting is not returned with anything better than their saying: "O Allah, You are Peace, and from You is peace. Blessed are You, O Possessor of majesty and honor." Then the Lord, blessed and exalted, reveals Himself to them, smiling at them, and says: "O people of Paradise!" The first thing they hear from Him, exalted, is: "Where are My servants who obeyed Me in the unseen and did not see Me? This is the Day of Increase." They gather upon one word: "We are pleased, so be pleased with us." He says: "O people of Paradise, if I were not pleased with you, I would not have made you dwell in My Paradise. This is the Day of Increase, so ask Me." They gather upon one word: "Show us Your Face that we may look upon it." Then the Lord, majestic in majesty, removes the veils for them and reveals Himself to them, and there envelops them of His light what, had Allah not decreed that they should not be burned, would have burned them. No one in that gathering remains without his Lord speaking with him in private conversation, to the point that He says: "O so-and-so, do you remember the day you did such and such?" reminding him of some of his lapses in the world. He says: "O Lord, did You not forgive me?" He says: "Yes, by My forgiveness you have reached this station." So how delightful to the ears is that private conversation, and how delightful to the eyes of the righteous is looking at the Face of the Generous in the Hereafter, and how humiliating for those who return with the losing bargain! ﴿Faces on that day radiant, looking at their Lord; and faces on that day frowning, thinking that a calamity will be inflicted upon them﴾.

The poet said:
"So come, O you who desire the Gardens of Eden, for they are your first dwellings, and therein is your tent.
But we are captives of the enemy; will we see ourselves return to our homelands and be safe?"

(Section)
When those granted success know what they were created for, and what their creation was intended for, they raise their heads, and behold, the banner of Paradise has been raised for them. They hasten toward it, and behold, its straight path has become clear to them, so they walk upon it steadily. They see that the greatest loss is selling what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived, for an everlasting duration that does not end or pass away, for a fleeting pleasure of life, which is only like confused dreams or a phantom visiting in sleep, mixed with turbidity and blended with choking. If it makes you laugh a little, it makes you weep much; if it gives you joy for a day, it saddens you for months. Its pains exceed its pleasures, its sorrows are many times its joys, it has fears, and its end is a pleasant union.

Alas, at a fool in the form of a wise man, and a madman in the garb of a reasonable person, who preferred the perishing, base fortune over the lasting, precious fortune, and sold a Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth for a narrow prison among the people of afflictions and calamities; and goodly dwellings in the Gardens of Eden beneath which rivers flow for narrow hovels whose end is ruin and destruction; and beautiful, equal-aged maidens, like rubies and coral, for filthy, polluted, evil-natured women, who are fornicators or take lovers; and cloistered Houris in tents, for corrupt women dispersed among people; and rivers of wine, a delight to drinkers, for a filthy, intoxicating drink that dulls the mind and corrupts this world and religion; and the delight of gazing upon the Face of the Mighty, the Merciful, for enjoying the sight of a hideous, repugnant face; and hearing speech from the Merciful, for hearing musical instruments, singing, and melodies; and sitting on pulpits of pearl, ruby, and chrysolite on the Day of Increase, for sitting in gatherings of wickedness with every rebellious devil; and the caller's cry, "O people of Paradise, you shall have bliss and not despair; you shall live and not die; you shall abide and not depart; you shall be young and not grow old," for the singing of singers:
"Love has stopped me where you are, and I have neither one who lags behind it nor one who goes ahead of it.
I find blame in your love sweet, out of love for your remembrance, so let the blamers blame me."

This sale's gross loss will only become clear on the Day of Resurrection, and the folly of its seller will only become evident on the Day of Regret and Remorse, when ﴿the righteous are gathered to the Most Merciful as honored guests﴾ and ﴿the criminals are driven to Hell like thirsty cattle﴾. The one who calls out will proclaim before all witnesses that the people of the Standing Place should know who among the servants is most deserving of nobility. If the one who lagged behind this company were to imagine what Allah has prepared for them of honor, what He has stored up for them of grace and bounty, and what He has hidden for them of joy for the eyes, which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived, he would know what merchandise he squandered, that there is no good for him in his life, and that he is counted among the discarded goods. He would know that those people have attained a great dominion that is not subject to calamities and does not cease, and that they have won everlasting bliss in the neighborhood of the Great, the Exalted.

So they will recline in the gardens of Paradise, sitting on its couches beneath canopies, reclining on cushions whose linings are of brocade, delighting in the maidens with large dark eyes, and enjoying every kind of fruit. ﴿Youths made eternal will circulate among them with goblets, jugs, and a cup from a flowing spring; it will neither cause them headache nor leave them intoxicated﴾, ﴿and fruit of whatever they choose, and the flesh of birds of whatever they desire﴾, ﴿and maidens with large dark eyes, like hidden pearls, as a reward for what they used to do﴾. ﴿They will be served with platters of gold and goblets, and therein is whatever the souls desire and whatever delights the eyes, and you will abide therein forever﴾.

By Allah, it has been proclaimed for her in the market of slump, yet no heart has inclined to her nor sought her, except a few of the servants. How strange! How could her seeker sleep, and how could her suitor withhold her dowry? How could life be sweet in this world after hearing her reports? How could the one who longs for her find rest without embracing her virgins? How could the eyes of the yearning find comfort without her? How could the souls of the certain endure patience without her? How could the hearts of most of mankind turn away from her? And with what could the souls of those who turned away be compensated for her?

Poetry describing Paradise:

That is only out of jealousy, that anyone other than her equal should attain her, and the Lord knows best of creation.
Even if she is veiled from us with every hateful thing, and surrounded by what harms and pains the souls,
Then to Allah belongs what is within her of delight, and kinds of pleasures in which one may enjoy himself.
And to Allah belongs the cool life between her tents and her gardens, and the smile of the flower in the meadow.
And to Allah belongs her valley, which is the promised place for the seekers, for the delegation of lovers, if only you were among them.
In its valleys, one wanders in ecstatic longing, a lover who sees that ecstatic longing is a gain.
And to Allah belong the joys of the lovers when He addresses them from above and greets them.
And to Allah belong the eyes that see Allah openly, on which neither injustice falls nor do they grow weary.
O glance that brought freshness to the face, after it, can the lover who is smitten be consoled?
And to Allah, how many a beauty, when she smiles, a light brighter than the dawn shines for her.
O delight of the eyes when she turns toward them, and O delight of the ears when she speaks!
O shame of the moist branch when it bends, and O shame of the two dawns when she smiles!
If you are one with a heart sick from her love, nothing remains but her union, which is your balm.
Especially in kissing her when embracing her, and when a bracelet has come to be under your neck from her.
You see him, when she reveals to him the beauty of her face, delighting in her before union, and taking pleasure.
The eye enjoys fruit when it beholds her, fruits of various kinds whose clusters never fail.
Clusters from a vine, apples of Paradise, and pomegranates, branches for which the heart is enamored.
For the rose is what her cheeks have clothed, and for the wine is what her saliva and mouth have mingled.
She divides beauty into one gathered whole, so how strange is it that one should be divided into many!
For her are scattered parts of beauty, gathered together in their totality, and indeed forgetting her is forbidden.
She reminds one of the Most Merciful through the one who looks, and he speaks in glorification without stammering.
When she confronts the army of sorrows with her face, the army turns back in defeat upon its heels.
O suitor of the beautiful one, if you are desirous, this is the time of dowry, and it is the one that comes first.
When the water of youth flowed through her branch, he was certain that he truly would never grow old.
Be hateful to the unfaithful women for her love, and you will be favored with her above them, and enjoy her.
And be whoever desires someone other than her, for she, for someone like you, is widowed in the Gardens of Eden.
Fast your nearest day, perhaps tomorrow you will attain the festival of Eid, while people are fasting.
Advance, and do not be content with a troubled life, for whoever does not advance does not win pleasures.
And even if the world becomes narrow upon you in its entirety, and there is no dwelling in it known to you,
Then come to the Gardens of Eden, for its first dwellings are there, and therein is the encampment.
But we are captives of the enemy; will we ever return to our homelands and be safe?
They claim that the stranger, when he goes far away and his homeland is distant from him, is in debt.
And what estrangement is greater than our estrangement, in which the enemies have come to rule over us?
Come to the market where the lovers meet; that market is known to the people.
Take from it whatever you wish without price, for the merchants have already advanced and submitted in it.
Come to the day of increase, on which is the visit of the Lord of the Throne; today is a festival.
Come to a vast valley there, whose soil is better than the most fragrant musk.
There are pulpits of light there, of silver, and of pure gold, which will not break.
And mounds of musk that have been made as seats for those below the people of the pulpits, which is known.
So while they are in their life and their joy, and their provisions flow to them and are apportioned to them,
Behold them in a shining light by which the gardens are illuminated in all their regions, not imagined.
The Lord of the heavens manifests Himself to them openly, and He laughs above the Throne, then speaks.
Peace be upon you; all of them hear with their ears His greeting as He greets.
He says: Ask Me for whatever you desire, for everything you want is with Me, for I am the Most Merciful.
They all say: We ask You for Your pleasure, for You are the One who bestows beauty and shows mercy.
So He gives to them this, and all of them bear witness against Him, exalted is Allah, for Allah is most generous.
O seller of this for a hasty, paltry price, as if you do not know. Yes, you will come to know.
But if you do not know, that is a calamity; and if you do know, the calamity is greater.

(Fa'ida)

The gasp (shahqa, a sudden cry or sob of ecstatic emotion) that occurs upon hearing the Qur'an or other things has causes:

First, a station appears to him upon hearing that is not his, so he is delighted by it, and the gasp arises in him. This is the gasp of longing.

Second, a sin he has committed appears to him, so he gasps out of fear and grief for himself. This is the gasp of fear.

Third, a deficiency in himself appears to him that he cannot remove, so this grief arises in him, and he gasps with the gasp of sorrow.

Fourth, the perfection of his beloved appears to him while he sees the path to it blocked from him, so this produces a gasp of regret and sorrow.

Fifth, his beloved has been hidden from him and he has been occupied with other things, then the listening reminds him of his beloved, so his beauty shines upon him and he sees the door open and the path clear, and he gasps in joy and delight at what has appeared.

In every case, the cause of the gasp is the strength of the incoming state and the weakness of the vessel in bearing it. Strength is for that incoming state to work its effect inwardly without appearing outwardly, and this is stronger for him and more lasting, for when he manifests it, its effect weakens and its cessation draws near. This is the ruling on the gasp from the sincere one, for the one who gasps is either sincere, or a thief, or a hypocrite.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 32, verses 16–17 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted said concerning the lovers (al-muhibbin): ﴿Their sides forsake their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and in hope﴾.

When their sides forsook their beds, the sides (of the body) forsook them, and they made them serve, and commanded them, and they obeyed.

The poet said:
"My day is the day of people, until, when night appears to me, the beds draw me to you."

It is related that one of the righteous passed by a mosque and saw Satan standing at its door, unable to enter. He looked, and there was a man sleeping and another standing in prayer. He said to him: "Does this one who prays prevent you from entering?" He said: "No, it is that crouching lion that prevents me. Were it not for his place, I would have entered."

In sum, the heart of the lover is always on a journey without end toward his Beloved. Whenever he crosses one stage and station, another appears to him, as it has been said:
"When you cross one sign, another sign appears."

He is a traveler among his family, a wayfarer while in his home, and a stranger while among his brothers and kin. He sees everyone as belonging to him, yet he does not see himself as belonging to anyone. The strength of the lover's attachment to his Beloved requires that his heart not settle short of reaching Him. Whenever his movements calm and his preoccupations lessen, the affairs of his heart gather upon him, and indeed his journey toward his Beloved grows stronger.

(Admonition)
A journey is only completed, and the traveler only arrives, by keeping to the highway and traveling by night. If the traveler strays from the road and sleeps the whole night, when will he reach his destination?

(Section: That Paradise is beyond what occurs to the mind or what passes through the imagination)
And that the place of a whip's length in it is better than the world and what is in it.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and in hope, and from what We have provided them they spend. No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do﴾.

Consider how He matched what they hid of night prayer with the reward He hid for them, which no soul knows. And how He matched their anxiety, fear, and restlessness upon their beds, when they rise for the night prayer, with the coolness of eyes in Paradise.

In the Two Sahihs (al-Sahihayn, Bukhari and Muslim), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, Allah the Mighty and Majestic said:
"I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived."
The confirmation of this in the Book of Allah is: ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do﴾.

In another wording in both: Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: "I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived, as a treasure, apart from what I have revealed to you." Then he recited: ﴿No soul knows﴾.

In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi, who said: "I witnessed with the Prophet (ﷺ) a gathering in which Paradise was described, until he finished. Then he said at the end of his speech about it: 'what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.' Then he recited this verse: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and in hope, and from what We have provided them they spend. No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do﴾."

In the Two Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:
"A bow's length of one of you in Paradise is better than what the sun rises upon or sets upon."

The hadith of Abu Umamah from the Prophet (ﷺ) has already preceded: "Whoever exerts himself for Paradise, for by the Lord of the Ka'bah, Paradise has no equal. It is a light that shines, a fragrant herb that sways, a lofty palace, a flowing river, ripe fruit, a beautiful and lovely spouse, many garments, a dwelling forever in an abode of peace, fruits, greenery, joy, blessing, and an elevated, radiant dwelling." And if there were nothing of Paradise's worth and nobility except that it is not asked for by the Face of Allah other than itself, that would be a sufficient honor and virtue.

And as in Sunan Abi Dawud, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn Mu'adh ibn al-Mundhir, from Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:
"Nothing is asked by the Face of Allah except Paradise."

In Mu'jam al-Tabarani, from the hadith of Baqiyyah, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:
"When Allah created the Garden of Eden, He created in it what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. Then He said to it: 'Speak.' It said: 'The believers have indeed prospered.'"

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "A place of a whip in Paradise is better than the world and what is in it."

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, Hammam narrated to us from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:
"The lash of one of your whips in Paradise is better than what is between the heaven and the earth."
And this chain is according to the conditions of the Two Sahihs.

Al-Tirmidhi said: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Ibn Lahi'ah informed us from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Dawud ibn 'Amir ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said:
"If the smallest fingernail of what is in Paradise appeared, it would adorn everything between the horizons of the heavens and the earth. And if a man of the people of Paradise looked out and his bracelets appeared, he would obscure the light of the sun as the sun obscures the light of the stars."
Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan gharib hadith. We do not know it with this chain except from the hadith of Ibn Lahi'ah.
Yahya ibn Ayyub has narrated this hadith from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, and said from Amr ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from the Prophet (ﷺ).
I say: Ibn Wahb has also narrated it: Amr, that is Ibn al-Harith, informed us that Sulayman ibn Humayd narrated to him that 'Amir ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas said, Sulayman said: "I do not know except that he narrated to me from his father, from the Messenger of Allah, from the Messenger of Allah, that he said:
'If a fingernail of Paradise appeared to the world, it would adorn what is between the heaven and the earth.'"
And on this topic there are reports from Anas ibn Malik, Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, and 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As.

How can the worth of an abode be measured, which Allah planted with His Hand, made a dwelling for His beloved ones, and filled with His mercy, honors, and good pleasure? He described its bliss as the great triumph, its kingdom as the great dominion, deposited in it all good in its entirety, and purified it from every defect, blemish, and deficiency.

If you ask about its earth and soil, it is musk and saffron. If you ask about its ceiling, it is the Throne of the Merciful. If you ask about its paving, it is pure musk. If you ask about its pebbles, they are pearls and gems. If you ask about its building, it is a brick of silver and a brick of gold. If you ask about its trees, there is no tree whose trunk is not of gold and silver, not of firewood or timber. If you ask about its fruit, it is like large jars, softer than butter and sweeter than honey. If you ask about its leaves, they are finer than the most delicate garments. If you ask about its rivers, they are rivers of milk whose taste never changes, rivers of wine, a delight for drinkers, and rivers of purified honey. If you ask about their food, it is fruit of their choosing and the flesh of birds they desire. If you ask about their drink, it is Tasnim, ginger, and camphor. If you ask about their vessels, they are vessels of gold and silver in the clarity of crystal. If you ask about the width of its doors, between the two panels is a forty years' journey, and a day will come upon it when it is crowded with throngs. If you ask about the rustling of the winds in its trees, they stir delight in whoever hears them. If you ask about its shade, there is one tree under whose shade a swift, vigorous rider travels for a hundred years without crossing it. If you ask about its vastness, its least inhabitant moves through his kingdom, couches, palaces, and gardens for a distance of two thousand years. If you ask about its tents and domes, one tent is a hollow pearl, sixty miles long, among those tents. If you ask about its high chambers and pavilions, they are upper rooms above upper rooms, built, with rivers flowing beneath them. If you ask about its height, look at the star rising or setting on the horizon that eyes can hardly reach. If you ask about the clothing of its people, it is silk and gold. If you ask about their bedding, its linings are of thick brocade, spread out in the highest ranks. If you ask about their couches, they are beds with canopies, which are curtained chambers fastened with golden buttons, having no gaps or crevices. If you ask about the faces of its people and their beauty, they are in the form of the moon. If you ask about their teeth, they are the sons of thirty-three, in the form of Adam, peace be upon him, the father of mankind. If you ask about their listening, it is the singing of their wives, the Wide-eyed Houris, and above that the hearing of the voices of the angels and the prophets, and above both, the speech of the Lord of the worlds. If you ask about their mounts on which they visit one another, they are swift camels, by Allah's will, that carry them wherever they wish in the gardens. If you ask about their ornaments and emblems, they are bracelets of gold and pearls, and on their heads are crowns. If you ask about their young servants, they are everlasting youths, as if they were hidden pearls. If you ask about their brides and spouses, they are the full-breasted maidens of equal age, through whose limbs the water of youth flows. For the rose and the apple is what their cheeks wear, for the pomegranate is what their breasts hold, for the strung pearls is what their mouths contain, and for delicacy and slenderness is what their waists encircle. The sun runs through the beauties of their faces when they appear, and lightning flashes between their front teeth when they smile. When she faces her lover, say whatever you wish about the meeting of two luminaries; and when she speaks to him, what do you imagine of the conversation of two beloveds? If she embraces him, what do you imagine of the entwining of two branches? He sees his face in the cheek of her, as one sees in a mirror that its polisher has burnished. He sees the marrow of her shin through the flesh; neither her skin nor her bone nor her garments conceal it. If she looked out upon the world, she would fill what is between the earth and the heaven with fragrance, make the mouths of creation utter tahlil, takbir, and tasbih, adorn what is between the two horizons, and cause every eye to look away from all else, and she would obscure the light of the sun as the sun obscures the light of the stars. She would have greeted with the living, self-subsisting Allah all who stand upon her back. Her veil upon her head is better than the world and what is in it, and her union is more desirable to him than all his wishes. She does not increase over the long ages except in beauty and loveliness, and the length of time only increases her in love and union. She is free from menstruation, childbirth, the monthly course, and postnatal bleeding, purified from mucus, spittle, urine, feces, and all other impurities. Her youth does not fade, her garments do not wear out, the garment of her beauty does not decay, and the sweetness of her union does not bore. She has restricted her gaze to her husband, so she does not look at anyone else, and he has restricted his gaze to her; she is the ultimate object of his wish and desire. If he looks at her, she delights him; if he commands her to obey him, she obeys him; if he is absent from her, she guards him. So she is with him in the ultimate of hopes and security. Moreover, no human or jinn has touched her before him. Whenever he looks at her, she fills his heart with joy, and whenever she speaks to him, she fills his ear with scattered and arranged pearls. When she appears, she fills the palace and the upper chamber with light. If you ask about her age, she is of equal age in the finest prime of youth. If you ask about beauty, have you seen the sun and the moon? If you ask about her eyes, they are the most beautiful black in the clearest white, with the most lovely gaze. If you ask about her stature, have you seen the finest branches? If you ask about her breasts, they are full-breasted maidens whose breasts are like the tenderest pomegranates. If you ask about her complexion, it is like the ruby and coral. If you ask about the beauty of her character, they are the good, beautiful women who combine beauty with kindness, given the beauty of inner and outer self, so they are the joy of souls and the coolness of eyes. If you ask about the goodness of companionship and the pleasure found there, they are the women who make themselves beloved to their husbands with a gentle affection that blends with the spirit in a manner beyond description. So what do you imagine of a woman who, when she laughs in the face of her husband, lights up Paradise with her laughter, and when she moves from one palace to another, you would say: this is the sun moving through the constellations of its sphere? When she is in the presence of her husband, how sweet is that presence, and if she embraces him, how delightful is that embrace and close contact!
Their poet said:
"Her talk is lawful magic; if it had not produced the killing of the cautious Muslim,
If it lasts long, it does not weary; and if she speaks, the speaker wishes she did not finish."
If she sings, how delightful to sight and hearing! If she is companionable and delights, how sweet that companionship and delight! If she kisses, nothing is more desirable to him than that kiss; if she gives, nothing is sweeter or better than that giving. Moreover, if you ask about the Day of Increase (yawm al-mazid), the increase of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy, and the vision of His Face, which is exalted above likeness and resemblance, as you see the sun at midday and the moon on the night of the full moon, as the truthful and believed one (al-sadiq al-masduq) has transmitted reports about it, this is found in the sound collections, the Sunan, and the Musnads, from the narrations of Jarir, Suhayb, Anas, Abu Hurayrah, and Abu Musa and Abu Sa'id. So listen: on the day when the caller calls, "O people of Paradise! Your Lord, blessed and exalted, wishes to visit you, so come to His visitation." They will say: "We hear and obey." They will rise hastening to the visitation, and behold, swift camels have been prepared for them. They mount them swiftly, until they reach the spacious valley that was made their appointment. They gather there, and the caller leaves none of them behind. The Lord, blessed and exalted, commands His Throne, and it is set up there. Then pulpits of light are set up for them, pulpits of pearl, pulpits of chrysolite, pulpits of gold, and pulpits of silver. The least of them sits on mounds of musk, and far be it that anyone among them be lowly. They do not see that the owners of the thrones are above them in gifts. When their seats are settled and their places are at rest, the caller calls: "O people of Paradise! For you there is a promise with Allah which He wishes to fulfill for you." They will say: "What is it? Has He not whitened our faces, made our scales heavy, admitted us into Paradise, and removed us from the Fire?" While they are like that, a light shines upon them, and Paradise is illuminated by it. They raise their heads, and behold, the Almighty, exalted in majesty and sanctified in His names, has looked down upon them from above and said: "O people of Paradise, peace be upon you." This greeting is not returned with anything better than their saying: "O Allah, You are Peace, and from You is peace. Blessed are You, O Possessor of majesty and honor." Then the Lord, blessed and exalted, reveals Himself to them, smiling at them, and says: "O people of Paradise!" The first thing they hear from Him, exalted, is: "Where are My servants who obeyed Me in the unseen and did not see Me? This is the Day of Increase." They gather upon one word: "We are pleased, so be pleased with us." He says: "O people of Paradise, if I were not pleased with you, I would not have made you dwell in My Paradise. This is the Day of Increase, so ask Me." They gather upon one word: "Show us Your Face that we may look upon it." Then the Lord, majestic in majesty, removes the veils for them and reveals Himself to them, and there envelops them of His light what, had Allah not decreed that they should not be burned, would have burned them. No one in that gathering remains without his Lord speaking with him in private conversation, to the point that He says: "O so-and-so, do you remember the day you did such and such?" reminding him of some of his lapses in the world. He says: "O Lord, did You not forgive me?" He says: "Yes, by My forgiveness you have reached this station." So how delightful to the ears is that private conversation, and how delightful to the eyes of the righteous is looking at the Face of the Generous in the Hereafter, and how humiliating for those who return with the losing bargain! ﴿Faces on that day radiant, looking at their Lord; and faces on that day frowning, thinking that a calamity will be inflicted upon them﴾.

The poet said:
"So come, O you who desire the Gardens of Eden, for they are your first dwellings, and therein is your tent.
But we are captives of the enemy; will we see ourselves return to our homelands and be safe?"

(Section)
When those granted success know what they were created for, and what their creation was intended for, they raise their heads, and behold, the banner of Paradise has been raised for them. They hasten toward it, and behold, its straight path has become clear to them, so they walk upon it steadily. They see that the greatest loss is selling what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived, for an everlasting duration that does not end or pass away, for a fleeting pleasure of life, which is only like confused dreams or a phantom visiting in sleep, mixed with turbidity and blended with choking. If it makes you laugh a little, it makes you weep much; if it gives you joy for a day, it saddens you for months. Its pains exceed its pleasures, its sorrows are many times its joys, it has fears, and its end is a pleasant union.

Alas, at a fool in the form of a wise man, and a madman in the garb of a reasonable person, who preferred the perishing, base fortune over the lasting, precious fortune, and sold a Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth for a narrow prison among the people of afflictions and calamities; and goodly dwellings in the Gardens of Eden beneath which rivers flow for narrow hovels whose end is ruin and destruction; and beautiful, equal-aged maidens, like rubies and coral, for filthy, polluted, evil-natured women, who are fornicators or take lovers; and cloistered Houris in tents, for corrupt women dispersed among people; and rivers of wine, a delight to drinkers, for a filthy, intoxicating drink that dulls the mind and corrupts this world and religion; and the delight of gazing upon the Face of the Mighty, the Merciful, for enjoying the sight of a hideous, repugnant face; and hearing speech from the Merciful, for hearing musical instruments, singing, and melodies; and sitting on pulpits of pearl, ruby, and chrysolite on the Day of Increase, for sitting in gatherings of wickedness with every rebellious devil; and the caller's cry, "O people of Paradise, you shall have bliss and not despair; you shall live and not die; you shall abide and not depart; you shall be young and not grow old," for the singing of singers:
"Love has stopped me where you are, and I have neither one who lags behind it nor one who goes ahead of it.
I find blame in your love sweet, out of love for your remembrance, so let the blamers blame me."

This sale's gross loss will only become clear on the Day of Resurrection, and the folly of its seller will only become evident on the Day of Regret and Remorse, when ﴿the righteous are gathered to the Most Merciful as honored guests﴾ and ﴿the criminals are driven to Hell like thirsty cattle﴾. The one who calls out will proclaim before all witnesses that the people of the Standing Place should know who among the servants is most deserving of nobility. If the one who lagged behind this company were to imagine what Allah has prepared for them of honor, what He has stored up for them of grace and bounty, and what He has hidden for them of joy for the eyes, which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived, he would know what merchandise he squandered, that there is no good for him in his life, and that he is counted among the discarded goods. He would know that those people have attained a great dominion that is not subject to calamities and does not cease, and that they have won everlasting bliss in the neighborhood of the Great, the Exalted.

So they will recline in the gardens of Paradise, sitting on its couches beneath canopies, reclining on cushions whose linings are of brocade, delighting in the maidens with large dark eyes, and enjoying every kind of fruit. ﴿Youths made eternal will circulate among them with goblets, jugs, and a cup from a flowing spring; it will neither cause them headache nor leave them intoxicated﴾, ﴿and fruit of whatever they choose, and the flesh of birds of whatever they desire﴾, ﴿and maidens with large dark eyes, like hidden pearls, as a reward for what they used to do﴾. ﴿They will be served with platters of gold and goblets, and therein is whatever the souls desire and whatever delights the eyes, and you will abide therein forever﴾.

By Allah, it has been proclaimed for her in the market of slump, yet no heart has inclined to her nor sought her, except a few of the servants. How strange! How could her seeker sleep, and how could her suitor withhold her dowry? How could life be sweet in this world after hearing her reports? How could the one who longs for her find rest without embracing her virgins? How could the eyes of the yearning find comfort without her? How could the souls of the certain endure patience without her? How could the hearts of most of mankind turn away from her? And with what could the souls of those who turned away be compensated for her?

Poetry describing Paradise:

That is only out of jealousy, that anyone other than her equal should attain her, and the Lord knows best of creation.
Even if she is veiled from us with every hateful thing, and surrounded by what harms and pains the souls,
Then to Allah belongs what is within her of delight, and kinds of pleasures in which one may enjoy himself.
And to Allah belongs the cool life between her tents and her gardens, and the smile of the flower in the meadow.
And to Allah belongs her valley, which is the promised place for the seekers, for the delegation of lovers, if only you were among them.
In its valleys, one wanders in ecstatic longing, a lover who sees that ecstatic longing is a gain.
And to Allah belong the joys of the lovers when He addresses them from above and greets them.
And to Allah belong the eyes that see Allah openly, on which neither injustice falls nor do they grow weary.
O glance that brought freshness to the face, after it, can the lover who is smitten be consoled?
And to Allah, how many a beauty, when she smiles, a light brighter than the dawn shines for her.
O delight of the eyes when she turns toward them, and O delight of the ears when she speaks!
O shame of the moist branch when it bends, and O shame of the two dawns when she smiles!
If you are one with a heart sick from her love, nothing remains but her union, which is your balm.
Especially in kissing her when embracing her, and when a bracelet has come to be under your neck from her.
You see him, when she reveals to him the beauty of her face, delighting in her before union, and taking pleasure.
The eye enjoys fruit when it beholds her, fruits of various kinds whose clusters never fail.
Clusters from a vine, apples of Paradise, and pomegranates, branches for which the heart is enamored.
For the rose is what her cheeks have clothed, and for the wine is what her saliva and mouth have mingled.
She divides beauty into one gathered whole, so how strange is it that one should be divided into many!
For her are scattered parts of beauty, gathered together in their totality, and indeed forgetting her is forbidden.
She reminds one of the Most Merciful through the one who looks, and he speaks in glorification without stammering.
When she confronts the army of sorrows with her face, the army turns back in defeat upon its heels.
O suitor of the beautiful one, if you are desirous, this is the time of dowry, and it is the one that comes first.
When the water of youth flowed through her branch, he was certain that he truly would never grow old.
Be hateful to the unfaithful women for her love, and you will be favored with her above them, and enjoy her.
And be whoever desires someone other than her, for she, for someone like you, is widowed in the Gardens of Eden.
Fast your nearest day, perhaps tomorrow you will attain the festival of Eid, while people are fasting.
Advance, and do not be content with a troubled life, for whoever does not advance does not win pleasures.
And even if the world becomes narrow upon you in its entirety, and there is no dwelling in it known to you,
Then come to the Gardens of Eden, for its first dwellings are there, and therein is the encampment.
But we are captives of the enemy; will we ever return to our homelands and be safe?
They claim that the stranger, when he goes far away and his homeland is distant from him, is in debt.
And what estrangement is greater than our estrangement, in which the enemies have come to rule over us?
Come to the market where the lovers meet; that market is known to the people.
Take from it whatever you wish without price, for the merchants have already advanced and submitted in it.
Come to the day of increase, on which is the visit of the Lord of the Throne; today is a festival.
Come to a vast valley there, whose soil is better than the most fragrant musk.
There are pulpits of light there, of silver, and of pure gold, which will not break.
And mounds of musk that have been made as seats for those below the people of the pulpits, which is known.
So while they are in their life and their joy, and their provisions flow to them and are apportioned to them,
Behold them in a shining light by which the gardens are illuminated in all their regions, not imagined.
The Lord of the heavens manifests Himself to them openly, and He laughs above the Throne, then speaks.
Peace be upon you; all of them hear with their ears His greeting as He greets.
He says: Ask Me for whatever you desire, for everything you want is with Me, for I am the Most Merciful.
They all say: We ask You for Your pleasure, for You are the One who bestows beauty and shows mercy.
So He gives to them this, and all of them bear witness against Him, exalted is Allah, for Allah is most generous.
O seller of this for a hasty, paltry price, as if you do not know. Yes, you will come to know.
But if you do not know, that is a calamity; and if you do know, the calamity is greater.

(Fa'ida)

The gasp (shahqa, a sudden cry or sob of ecstatic emotion) that occurs upon hearing the Qur'an or other things has causes:

First, a station appears to him upon hearing that is not his, so he is delighted by it, and the gasp arises in him. This is the gasp of longing.

Second, a sin he has committed appears to him, so he gasps out of fear and grief for himself. This is the gasp of fear.

Third, a deficiency in himself appears to him that he cannot remove, so this grief arises in him, and he gasps with the gasp of sorrow.

Fourth, the perfection of his beloved appears to him while he sees the path to it blocked from him, so this produces a gasp of regret and sorrow.

Fifth, his beloved has been hidden from him and he has been occupied with other things, then the listening reminds him of his beloved, so his beauty shines upon him and he sees the door open and the path clear, and he gasps in joy and delight at what has appeared.

In every case, the cause of the gasp is the strength of the incoming state and the weakness of the vessel in bearing it. Strength is for that incoming state to work its effect inwardly without appearing outwardly, and this is stronger for him and more lasting, for when he manifests it, its effect weakens and its cessation draws near. This is the ruling on the gasp from the sincere one, for the one who gasps is either sincere, or a thief, or a hypocrite.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 32, verse 21:

Several scholars have cited this verse as evidence for the punishment of the grave, among them ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAbbas. There is, however, some question about using it as proof, because this is a punishment in this world, sought so that they would return from disbelief. This would not have been hidden from the scholar of the Ummah and interpreter of the Qur'an (tarjuman al-Qur'an). But it was his deep understanding of the Qur'an and the precision of his grasp of it that led him to derive from it the punishment of the grave. For Allah, glorified is He, informed that for them there are two punishments, a lesser (adna) and a greater (akbar). He informed that He makes them taste some of the lesser punishment so that they may return. This shows that a remainder of the lesser punishment is left for them, by which they will be punished after the punishment of this world. This is why He said "from the lesser punishment" (min al-ʿadhab al-adna), and did not say "and We will make them taste the lesser punishment." So reflect upon this.

This is similar to the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Then an opening is made for him toward the Fire, and there comes to him some of its heat and its scorching winds," and he did not say, "its heat and its scorching winds come to him." For what reached him was only a portion of that, and most of it remains for him. And what the enemies of Allah tasted in this world was only some of the punishment, while there remains for them what is greater than it.

Faith rests on two pillars, certainty (yaqin) and patience (sabr), which are the two pillars mentioned in the words of the Most High: ﴿And We made from among them leaders, guiding by Our command when they were patient and used to be certain of Our signs.﴾

Through certainty one knows the reality of the command and prohibition, and of reward and punishment. Through patience one carries out what he is commanded and restrains himself from what he is forbidden. One cannot attain belief that the commands and prohibitions come from Allah, and belief in reward and punishment, except through certainty; and one cannot persist in doing what is commanded and restraining oneself from what is forbidden except through patience. Thus patience becomes half of faith, and the second half is gratitude (shukr), which is shown by doing what He has commanded and by abandoning what He has forbidden.

[Chapter: On the Degrees of Jihad against Satan]

As for jihad against Satan, it has two degrees. The first is striving to repel the doubts and suspicions that he casts into the servant, which undermine faith.
The second is striving to repel the corrupt desires and appetites that he casts into him. The first kind of striving is followed by certainty, and the second is followed by patience.
The Most High said: ﴿And We made from among them leaders, guiding by Our command when they were patient and used to be certain of Our signs﴾ [al-Sajdah: 24].
So He informed that leadership in religion is attained only through patience and certainty. Patience repels appetites and corrupt desires, and certainty repels doubts and suspicions.

(Benefit)
The Most High's words concerning the companions of Moses: ﴿And We made from among them leaders, guiding by Our command when they were patient and used to be certain of Our signs﴾
He informed that He made them leaders whom those after them would follow, because of their patience and certainty, since leadership in religion is attained only through patience and certainty. The one who calls to Allah the Exalted cannot accomplish his task except through his certainty in the truth to which he calls, his insight into it, and his patience in carrying out the call to Allah, bearing the hardships of the call and restraining the self from whatever weakens his resolve and diminishes his determination. Whoever is in this position is among the leaders who guide by the command of the Most High. It is known that the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ) are more worthy and more entitled to this description than the companions of Moses; they are more complete in certainty and greater in patience than all the nations. Therefore they are the most entitled to the station of this leadership. This is a matter established beyond doubt by Allah's testimony for them and His praise of them, and by the Messenger's testimony that they are the best generation, and that they are the chosen of Allah and His elect. It is impossible for those of such a state that they should all err concerning the truth while the later generations attain it. Had this been possible, realities would be reversed, and the later generations would be leaders whose fatwas and sayings must be referred to. Just as this is impossible by sense and reason, it is impossible by the Sacred Law. And success is from Allah.

(Section)
Allah, glory be to Him, has informed that this leadership is attained only through patience and certainty, saying: ﴿And We made from among them leaders, guiding by Our command when they were patient and used to be certain of Our signs﴾
So through patience and certainty leadership in religion is attained.
It has been said: through patience regarding the world.
It has been said: through patience in trials.
It has been said: through patience regarding what is forbidden.
The correct view is that it is through patience in all of that: patience in performing Allah's obligations, patience in abstaining from His prohibitions, and patience in His decrees.
Glory be to Him, He combined patience and certainty, for they are the happiness of the servant, and the loss of them causes the loss of his happiness. The heart is visited by the passing thoughts of desires that oppose Allah's command and by the passing thoughts of doubts that oppose His report. Through patience desires are repelled, and through certainty doubts are repelled. Desire and doubt are both opposed to religion in every respect, and no one escapes the punishment of Allah except one who repels his desires by patience and his doubts by certainty. For this reason He informed of the nullification of the deeds of the people of desires and doubts, saying: ﴿Like those before you, who were stronger than you in power and greater in wealth and children. They enjoyed their share, and you enjoyed your share as those before you enjoyed their share, and you indulged in vain talk as they indulged.﴾ Here, "enjoying their share" is their enjoyment of their portion of desires. Then He said: "and you indulged as they indulged," and this is plunging into falsehood concerning the religion of Allah, which is the plunging of the people of doubts. Then He said: ﴿Those—their deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter, and those are the losers.﴾
So He made the nullification of deeds and loss dependent upon following desires, which is enjoying one's share, and following doubts, which is plunging into falsehood.

(Section)
Just as Allah, glory be to Him, made leadership in religion dependent upon patience and certainty, the verse also includes two other principles.
The first is the call to Allah and the guidance of His creation.
The second is their guidance by what He has commanded upon the tongue of His Messenger (ﷺ), not by the dictates of their intellects, opinions, policies, tastes, or the imitation of their predecessors without proof from Allah, for He said: ﴿guiding by Our command﴾.
So these are four principles contained in this verse:
The first is patience, which is restraining the self from Allah's prohibitions, restraining it upon His obligations, and restraining it from resentment and complaint regarding His decrees.
The second is certainty, which is firm, decisive faith free of doubt, hesitation, suspicion, or uncertainty, concerning the five principles that He mentioned in His words: ﴿It is not righteousness that you turn your faces toward the east or the west, but righteousness is in one who believes in Allah, the Last Day, the angels, the Book, and the prophets﴾
And in His words: ﴿And whoever disbelieves in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day has certainly strayed far astray﴾
And in His words: ﴿The Messenger believes in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and the believers. All believe in Allah, His angels, His books, and His messengers﴾
Belief in Allah and the Last Day is included in belief in the books and messengers. The Prophet (ﷺ) combined them in the hadith of Umar, in his saying: "Faith is that you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day." Whoever does not believe in these five principles is not a believer. Certainty means that faith in them is established until it becomes as if directly witnessed by the heart, seen by it; its relation to insight is like the relation of the sun and moon to sight. For this reason some of the Salaf said: "Certainty is the whole of faith."
The third is guiding people and calling them to Allah and His Messenger. The Most High said: ﴿And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah, does righteous deeds, and says, "Indeed, I am of the Muslims"?﴾
Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "This is the beloved of Allah, this is the friend of Allah, who submitted to Allah, acted in His obedience, and called the creation to Him." This type is the best of human kinds and highest in rank with Allah on the Day of Resurrection.
They are the exception from the losers, as the Most High said: ﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss, except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and enjoined one another to truth and enjoined one another to patience.﴾
So Allah swore that the human species is in loss, except one who perfects himself by faith and righteous deeds and perfects others by enjoining them to these. For this reason al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "If people reflected on Surat al-Asr alone, it would suffice them."
No one is truly a follower of the Messenger except one who calls to Allah with insight. The Most High said: ﴿Say, "This is my way; I invite to Allah with insight, I and whoever follows me."﴾
His words "I invite to Allah" explain the way he is upon; so his way and the way of his followers is the call to Allah. Whoever does not call to Allah is not upon his way.
